title: Report to the Secretary of the Treasury from the Treasury Borrowing Advisory Committee
body: November 4, 2026 Dear Mr. Secretary, Since the TBAC last met in early August, Treasury markets have repriced toward a higher path for interest rates, reflecting stronger economic activity and associated financing needs, persistent energy-supply disruptions, and the Federal Reserve’s initial rate hike and projections for further increases. The selloff in rates was led by the front end of the yield curve, with two-year yields rising by roughly 50bps and ten-year yields by roughly 40bps. The move accelerated in September and early October, with ten-year yields peaking around 5.4% and thirty-year yields around 5.7% in early October. Some of that increase has since reversed. A substantial part of the repricing reflected stronger U.S. economic activity through the summer despite higher energy prices and rising rates. Household spending remained resilient as gains in financial wealth and lower savings rates cushioned pressure on real incomes. Existing fixed-rate mortgages limited the increase in homeowners’ debt-service costs, even as higher rates on new borrowing weighed on housing activity. Meanwhile, strong investment in computing equipment, intellectual property, and data centers offset weakness in more rate-sensitive investment. The infrastructure buildout proved less sensitive to financing costs than traditional housing-led expansions. Related gains in construction and equipment manufacturing are becoming visible but have not yet generated a broad acceleration in employment. This resilience gave the Federal Reserve greater scope to respond to persistent inflation risks exacerbated by the energy shock. Supply disruptions that began over the summer have proved more persistent than initially expected, keeping crude and refined-product prices elevated through the quarter and feeding into transportation and freight costs. Headline CPI accelerated to 3.7% in September, with gasoline alone accounting for more than half of the monthly increase. Core CPI ran at 2.6% as fuel and freight costs passed through to other categories. The Federal Reserve responded in September by raising its target range by 25 basis points to 3.75%–4.00%. Chairman Warsh emphasized both the strengthening economy and insufficient progress on inflation, characterizing the decision as removing accommodation rather than making already restrictive financial conditions materially tighter. The September Summary of Economic Projections reinforced the higher-for-longer message: the median policy-rate projection rose to 4.1% for both year-end 2026 and year-end 2027, compared with 3.8% and 3.6%, respectively, in June. Markets continued to price approximately three additional rate increases over the coming year even as the Fed held rates steady in October. More recently, higher borrowing costs and emerging weakness in equity and credit markets have moderated expectations for the pace of tightening but not eliminated expectations for further increases. Several cross-market and technical developments came into play over the quarter: Term premium has risen less than yields this year, though the ten-year term premium showed some strain in the early fall. The Federal Reserve Bank of New York’s ACM model estimate of the ten-year term premium rose approximately 20bps in September. Interest rate implied volatility rose sharply, reflecting greater priced uncertainty and raising the cost of option-based protection against further yield increases. As yields rose and refinancing incentives diminished, mortgage durations extended, prompting convexity hedgers to reduce duration. Collateralized mortgage obligation floaters with coupon caps added to hedging pressures as forward-implied coupons approached their caps, likely increasing demand for intermediate-dated rates volatility. These flows likely amplified the initial selloff and increase in volatility, although the scope for further mortgage-duration extension diminished as yields moved higher. Stronger economic activity was also driving expectations of higher interest rates outside the United States. The European Central Bank and Bank of Japan raised policy rates over the period as markets priced a broader tightening cycle across major developed economies. Developments in European sovereign markets were also relevant for Treasuries, as fiscal and political uncertainty produced a sharp widening in French government-bond spreads, adding to volatility across global fixed-income markets. Those linkages have not operated uniformly: the correlation between French and U.S. yield changes weakened in October, and more acute French stress subsequently supported safe-haven demand for Treasuries and German Bunds. Technology-related financing remained an additional influence on capital markets and financial conditions. Large debt offerings and prospective mega-IPOs reflected substantial private-sector financing needs. Heavy technology issuance and uncertainty over future financing needs contributed to wider spreads in the sector and increased competition for long-duration capital. Banks and asset managers also helped technology companies tap a broader pool of capital through GPU-backed loans, equipment leases, and data center project financing. Foreign investor demand to finance U.S. technology contributed to dollar strength, providing an additional channel of financial tightening alongside higher borrowing costs. Although large issuance windows may influence Treasury concessions and hedging flows at the margin, there is no evidence of a persistent deterioration in Treasury auction demand. Recent auctions remained generally resilient, though individual results varied. Technology news also contributed to weaker risk sentiment later in the period, helping restore demand for Treasuries. By late October, the Nasdaq 100 had fallen just over 7% from its early-October high amid greater scrutiny of the returns on increasingly debt-financed technology investment. Together with wider credit spreads, the equity pullback helped restore a safe-haven bid for Treasuries, partially reversing the earlier rise in yields. Against that backdrop, the Committee convened for its quarterly refunding discussion. The outlook shows the funding gap widens over FY27 and increases further in FY28 and FY29. Consistent with Treasury’s cash management policy, Treasury recently published cash balance assumptions for the end of Q1 FY27 and Q2 FY27 at approximately $850 billion and $1 trillion, respectively. The Committee next addressed the first of its two charges: Super Intelligence (SI)-related issuance. Members discussed recent trends in corporate bond issuance related to SI and associated businesses. Members noted the market is in the midst of a significant technology financing cycle. Financing is also expanding beyond long-dated corporate bonds, with secured and asset-backed structures increasingly bringing issuance inside 10 years. Taken as a whole, the technology ecosystem appears to have both the capacity and incentive to sustain borrowing and investment. Foreign demand for U.S. fixed-income assets has accelerated this year, while the broader investor base retains significant capacity to absorb additional issuance. Insurers, pensions, households, and foreign investors provide diversified sources of demand, with households and private pensions still relatively under allocated to fixed income. Even modest reallocations from cash and equities could therefore absorb a meaningful share of projected borrowing. Treasury auction results show no evidence that 2026 technology-related issuance has crowded out long-end Treasury demand. To the extent technology investment is affecting rates, the Committee viewed the transmission as stemming from stronger growth rather than through crowding out. Higher Treasury yields have primarily reflected growth, policy expectations, and energy prices rather than an issuance-driven supply shock. Members emphasized, however, that the financing cycle remains in its early stages and recommended that Treasury continue to monitor potential effects on Treasury market demand as SI-related issuance grows. The Committee’s second charge focused on Treasury derivatives and their growing role in the market. Since the 2022 rise in yields, asset managers have increasingly used futures to gain synthetic Treasury exposure, while liability-driven investors, including pension funds and insurers, have used interest rate swaps to manage duration. The Committee emphasized that expressing duration through derivatives enhances demand for Treasuries by broadening market access and expanding intermediation capacity. In the context of discussing derivatives, the Committee identified several policy options that could further improve demand for cash Treasuries. These include easing regulatory constraints on balance sheet capacity, including exempting Treasuries from leverage ratios and recognizing pre-positioned discount window collateral in liquidity metrics; expanding access to repo financing; improving the availability of term repo; and enabling new entrants in repo market making. The Committee also recommended evaluation of fund accounting treatment of repo interest, tax treatment, and operational challenges. Together, these steps could broaden and diversify the base of cash Treasury holders, strengthen market intermediation, and support durable demand for Treasuries. The Committee discussed the efficacy of the liquidity support buyback program. There is a variety of evidence that the program has supported liquidity conditions since it was introduced in 2024, and buybacks remain an effective tool for that purpose. While an effective tool, the Committee believes that any management of Treasury’s maturity profile should be done via changes to auction sizes. To further the goal of financing the government at the lowest cost over time, the Committee continues to endorse an issuance strategy that balances expected costs and volatility of interest expense, matches issuance patterns to market demand, encourages smooth market functioning, and is regular and predictable. As members look ahead, baseline fiscal projections suggest that current auction sizes are likely to shift Treasury’s debt profile toward an increasing share of bill and shorter-term funding. The Committee believes that the market has recently been absorbing Treasury issuance well and that the bulk of recent interest rate rises reflect strong economic conditions and the monetary policy outlook rather than weak investor demand for Treasuries. The Committee discussed that real money investors, including retail and some institutional investors, have grown their demand as rates have risen and as a hedge against downward moves in economic conditions. However, the Committee also noted that money market fund assets have leveled off and the bill market has started to show some signs of price sensitivity. In light of that outlook, for the current quarter, the Committee recommended keeping nominal coupon, FRN, and TIPS auction sizes unchanged. However, the Committee believes that given current fiscal projections, increases in coupon auction sizes will be warranted later in FY27. Looking ahead, given the projected funding gaps in FY28 and FY29, members discussed different approaches to coupon increases over the horizon. While there is broad agreement across the Committee to increase coupon auction sizes, there was considerable debate around the pace and sizing specific to the long end of the curve. Members recommended that Treasury change its forward-guidance language and emphasized that clear communication alongside a regular and predictable operating framework remains important to help market participants adjust to future changes. In conclusion, consistent with its past messaging, the Committee encourages Congress to act to raise or suspend the debt limit to avoid disrupting Treasury market functioning, increasing costs to the taxpayer, and constraining economic growth. Respectfully, Jason S. Granet Chair, Treasury Borrowing Advisory Committee E. Alexander Schiller Vice Chair, Treasury Borrowing Advisory Committee

title: Quarterly Refunding Statement of Assistant Secretary for Financial Markets Hunter McMaster
body: November 4, 2026 WASHINGTON — The U.S. Department of the Treasury is offering $125 billion of Treasury securities to refund approximately $97 billion of privately-held Treasury notes and bonds maturing on November 15, 2026.  This issuance will raise new cash from private investors of approximately $28 billion.  The securities are: A 3-year note in the amount of $58 billion, maturing November 15, 2029; A 10-year note in the amount of $42 billion, maturing November 15, 2036; A 30-year bond in the amount of $25 billion, maturing November 15, 2056. The 3-year note will be auctioned at 1:00 p.m. ET on Monday, November 9, 2026.  The 10-year note will be auctioned at 1:00 p.m. ET on Tuesday, November 10, 2026.  The 30-year bond will be auctioned at 1:00 p.m. ET on Thursday, November 12, 2026.  All these auctions will take place on a yield basis and will settle on Monday, November 16, 2026. The balance of Treasury financing requirements over the quarter will be met with regular weekly bill auctions, cash management bills (CMBs), and monthly note, bond, Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities (TIPS), and 2-year Floating Rate Note (FRN) auctions. NOMINAL COUPON AND FRN FINANCING Treasury believes its current auction sizes leave it well positioned to address potential changes to the fiscal outlook and to the size and composition of the SOMA portfolio.  Based on current projected borrowing needs, Treasury anticipates maintaining nominal coupon and FRN auction sizes for the next several quarters.  Treasury is monitoring SOMA purchases of Treasury bills and growing demand for Treasury bills from the private sector.  Looking ahead, Treasury continues to evaluate potential future changes to nominal coupon and FRN auction sizes, with a focus on trends in structural demand and potential costs and risks of various issuance profiles.  As part of that process, Treasury will engage with a variety of market participants to better understand evolving Treasury supply and demand dynamics. In considering any changes, Treasury will be guided by the objective of financing the government at the lowest cost over time. The table below presents, in billions of dollars, the actual auction sizes for the August to October 2026 quarter and the anticipated auction sizes for the November 2026 to January 2027 quarter: 2-Year 3-Year 5-Year 7-Year 10-Year 20-Year 30-Year FRN Aug-26 69 58 70 44 42 16 25 28 Sep-26 69 58 70 44 39 13 22 28 Oct-26 69 58 70 44 39 13 22 30 Nov-26 69 58 70 44 42 16 25 28 Dec-26 69 58 70 44 39 13 22 28 Jan-27 69 58 70 44 39 13 22 30 Treasury plans to address any seasonal or unexpected variations in borrowing needs over the next quarter through changes in regular bill auction sizes and/or CMBs. TIPS FINANCING Over the November 2026 to January 2027 quarter, Treasury plans to maintain TIPS auction sizes at current levels: the November 10-year TIPS reopening auction size at $19 billion, the December 5-year TIPS reopening auction size at $24 billion, and the January 10-year TIPS new issue auction size at $21 billion. BILL ISSUANCE Treasury continues to see strong demand for bill securities from a broad range of market participants.  Based on current forecasts, Treasury expects to maintain current auction sizes of benchmark bills into late November and anticipates potentially issuing a short-dated CMB to meet its cash management needs around the end of November.  Given projections for receipts associated with the mid-December corporate and non-withheld tax date, Treasury expects to implement reductions to shorter-dated bill auction sizes during the month of December.  In January, Treasury anticipates increasing auction sizes across the bill curve based on expected seasonal fiscal outflows.  As always, Treasury will continue to evaluate near-term borrowing needs and assess additional adjustments to bill auction sizes as appropriate. CONVERSION OF 7-YEAR NOTE TO QUARTERLY NEW ISSUE Treasury plans to convert the 7-year note from a monthly new issue to a quarterly new issue with two reopenings (similar to the 10-year note).  The 7-year note will continue to be auctioned towards the end of each month and issue and mature at month end.  Treasury will auction new issues in March, June, September, and December and conduct reopening auctions in the subsequent two months of each cycle.  This conversion will go into effect beginning with the March 2027 new issue, which will be reopened in April and May. CASH BALANCE Treasury is assuming an $850 billion cash balance at the end of December.  However, based on current projections for the upcoming refunding quarter, Treasury estimates that the size of the Treasury General Account (TGA) could peak at $1.025 trillion (plus or minus $50 billion) in late November and late January.  These figures are consistent with Treasury’s long-standing cash balance policy and are driven by the large outflows expected to occur at those times. BUYBACKS Treasury is releasing a tentative buyback schedule for the upcoming refunding quarter.  Treasury anticipates that, over the course of the upcoming quarter, it will purchase up to $70 billion in off-the-run securities across buckets for liquidity support and up to $25 billion in the 1-month to 2-year maturity bucket for cash management purposes.  Treasury will continue to evaluate possible enhancements to buyback operations such as changes to maximum purchase amounts, buyback operation scheduling and frequency, security eligibility, and execution process. Please send comments or suggestions on these subjects or other subjects related to debt management to debt.management@treasury.gov . The next quarterly refunding announcement will take place on Wednesday, February 3, 2027. ###

title: Former Physician and Three Other Sex Offenders Indicted for Sharing Child Sexual Abuse Material While Serving Federal Prison Sentences in Atlanta
body: Press Release Former Physician and Three Other Sex Offenders Indicted for Sharing Child Sexual Abuse Material While Serving Federal Prison Sentences in Atlanta Wednesday, November 4, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Georgia ATLANTA – Justin Neisler was arraigned in federal court today on two counts of possessing child sexual abuse material (CSAM) while incarcerated at the Federal Correctional Institution in Atlanta (FCI Atlanta). This summer, three other FCI Atlanta inmates, Dustin Bishop, Jacob Breslin, and Harold Nuckols, were indicted on similar, related charges of possessing, receiving, and distributing CSAM and other obscene depictions of children while in custody. “Prison bars allegedly did not stop these defendants from re-victimizing innocent children for their perverted and depraved gratification,” said U.S. Attorney Theodore S. Hertzberg. “Contraband cell phones pose a clear risk to public safety, and my office will continue to arrest, prosecute, and seek additional prison time for inmates who commit new crimes, especially crimes involving child exploitation, while in custody.” “The exploitation of children is a horrific crime, and incarceration does not put an end to our responsibility to protect victims. These allegations demonstrate the lengths some offenders will go to continue their abuse, even behind prison walls,” said Marlo Graham, Special Agent in Charge of FBI Atlanta. “The FBI and our partners at the Bureau of Prisons will continue working together to identify, investigate, and hold accountable anyone who exploits children.” According to U.S. Attorney Hertzberg, the charges, and other information presented in court: In March 2026, Federal Bureau of Prisons (BOP) investigators at FCI Atlanta uncovered inmates who allegedly were receiving, possessing, and distributing CSAM amongst themselves. Bishop, who was serving a 10-year sentence for receipt of CSAM, and at least one other inmate allegedly obtained illegal, contraband cell phones and used them to search the dark web for CSAM. Bishop and others then downloaded the CSAM onto SD cards that inmates removed from MP3 players. Bishop and another inmate then allegedly used an SD card reader—another contraband item—to print the CSAM on the prison library copy machine, sometimes on the back of religious material. Bishop and another inmate then allegedly sold the CSAM to fellow inmates, including Breslin, who is serving a 15-year sentence for possessing and receiving CSAM. Bishop and another inmate also allegedly sold obscene depictions of fictious children engaged in sexually explicit conduct—including depictions of young Disney characters being sexually assaulted—to other inmates, including Nuckols, who is serving a more than 4-year sentence for possessing CSAM. In addition, under Neisler’s pillow, BOP investigators allegedly found a contraband cell phone containing CSAM. Neisler is a former Denver-based physician who is serving a 23-year prison sentence for producing CSAM. During the investigation, BOP investigators found approximately 450 CSAM images and videos at FCI Atlanta. Four defendants currently face charges from this investigation: Justin Neisler, 38, of Denver, Colorado, was arraigned today on federal charges of possession of CSAM. A grand jury indicted Neisler on October 27, 2026. Dustin Bishop, 38, of Raleigh, North Carolina, was arraigned on August 31, 2026, on federal charges of distribution of CSAM. A grand jury indicted Bishop on August 25, 2026. Jacob Breslin, 34, of Merritt Island, Florida, was arraigned on August 7, 2026, on federal charges of receipt and possession of CSAM. A grand jury indicted Breslin on July 28, 2026. Harold Nuckols, 29, of Henrico, Virginia, was arraigned on August 7, 2026, on federal charges of possessing obscene depictions of children engaged in sexually explicit conduct. A grand jury indicted Nuckols on July 28, 2026. If convicted, Neisler and Nuckols face at least 10 years, and Bishop and Breslin face at least 15 years, of imprisonment without the possibility of parole. The Court may order that any additional sentence be served consecutively to a sentence the defendant is currently serving. Members of the public are reminded that the indictments only contain charges.  The defendants are presumed innocent of the charges, and it will be the government’s burden to prove the defendants’ guilt beyond a reasonable doubt at trial. This case is being investigated by the Federal Bureau of Investigation, with valuable assistance provided by the Special Investigations Section of the Federal Bureau of Prisons. Assistant United States Attorney Matthew R. LaGrone is prosecuting the case. This case is being brought as part of Project Safe Childhood. In February 2006, the Attorney General launched Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative designed to protect children from online exploitation and abuse. Led by the United States Attorney’s Offices around the country, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state and local resources to apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.projectsafechildhood.gov. For further information please contact the U.S. Attorney’s Public Affairs Office at USAGAN.PressEmails@usdoj.gov or (404) 581-6185. The Internet address for the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Georgia is http://www.justice.gov/usao-ndga . Updated November 4, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Components Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - Georgia, Northern

title: Utah Minor Recovered by Law Enforcement After Oregon Man Allegedly Transported the Victim to Engage in Criminal Sexual Activity
body: Press Release Utah Minor Recovered by Law Enforcement After Oregon Man Allegedly Transported the Victim to Engage in Criminal Sexual Activity Wednesday, November 4, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Utah SALT LAKE CITY, Utah — An Oregon man is now in federal custody and charged in a criminal complaint with transportation with intent to engage in criminal sexual activity after he allegedly met a Utah minor online in May 2025, drove to Utah to pick up the victim, and then transported the victim to his residence across state lines.  The minor was recovered by law enforcement at the residence on Nov. 1. “Anyone engaged in the sexual exploitation of a minor will be held accountable,” said Attorney General Todd Blanche. “Today’s arrest is the first step toward bringing the accused to justice and relieving the pain endured by the victim and her family. This Department of Justice will never stop investigating and prosecuting individuals engaged in vicious predatory behavior.” “This individual is charged with transporting a minor to another state to engage in criminal sexual activity, a minor who was missing for a year and a half until Oregon police recovered her based on information provided by the FBI,” said FBI Director Kash Patel. “According to the criminal complaint the minor was groomed on gaming platforms and engaged in acts of self-harm and sexually explicit activity. To anyone targeting and exploiting children: this FBI and our partners are coming for you. We are using every tool at our disposal to combat nihilistic violent extremism, bring offenders to justice, and protect America’s most vulnerable. I want to thank the FBI Salt Lake Field Office, the Oregon State Police, and federal prosecutors for their outstanding work on this case.” “Our priority in this case was the safe return of the minor victim,” said U.S. Attorney Melissa Holyoak for the District of Utah. “Those who allegedly exploit and prey upon the most vulnerable members of our communities will be relentlessly investigated and held accountable. I want to thank the FBI and our local law enforcement partners in Oregon for their swift efforts to safely recover the victim and for their continued partnership as we pursue justice for the victim and the victim’s family.” Adam Hunter Harmel, 39, of Huntington, Oregon, was charged in a federal complaint on Nov. 2 in the District of Utah. He had his initial appearance on the complaint on Nov. 4 at the U.S. District Courthouse in Boise, Idaho. According to court documents, beginning in or about May 2025 and continuing until Nov. 1, in the District of Utah and elsewhere, Harmel allegedly transported the minor victim with the intent to engage in sexual activity with the victim. On or about Aug. 20, 2025, FBI Salt Lake City received information that the minor victim had disappeared in May 2025. During the investigation, the FBI learned that the minor victim was allegedly groomed on gaming platforms that are commonly used by Nihilistic Violent Extremist (NVE) Groups members to solicit sexually explicit photos and maiming photos. The grooming then transitioned to other social media applications. On Nov. 1, the FBI received a tip about the possible location of the minor victim and that the victim met Harmel on a social media application in May 2025. As alleged in court documents, Harmel kept a knife under his pillow to prevent the minor victim from escaping. The case is being investigated by the FBI Salt Lake City Field Office in conjunction with the FBI Joint Terrorism Task Force. Valuable assistance was provided by the Oregon State Police. Assistant U.S. Attorney Jawayria Z. Auchter for the District of Utah and Trial Attorneys Justin Sher and James Donnelly of the National Security Division’s Counterterrorism Section are prosecuting the case. A complaint is merely an allegation, and all defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. Updated November 4, 2026 Topic National Security Components Office of the Attorney General Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) National Security Division (NSD) USAO - Utah Press Release Number: 26-115

title: Shiprock Man Pleads Guilty After Shooting into Residence
body: Press Release Shiprock Man Pleads Guilty After Shooting into Residence Wednesday, November 4, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of New Mexico ALBUQUERQUE – A Shiprock man pleaded guilty to federal firearms offenses for shooting multiple rounds into an occupied residence. According to court documents, on January 21, 2026, Navajo Police Department dispatch received a call reporting that Taylon Keeswood , 20, an enrolled member of the Navajo Nation, was shooting at a house in Shiprock, New Mexico. Responding officers located and detained Keeswood near the house shortly after the call. Investigators recovered shell casings and confirmed that the residence, which was occupied by an adult and three children, had been struck numerous times by gunfire. No one inside the home was injured. Keeswood later admitted to investigators that he fired an AK-style rifle from his hip, emptying a 30-round magazine at the residence, which he believed belonged to an individual with whom he had prior disputes. After the shooting, Keeswood fled the area and hid the firearm, which law enforcement later recovered at a location he identified. Keeswood pleaded guilty to using and carrying a firearm during and in relation to a crime of violence. At sentencing Keeswood faces up to 10 years in prison. First Assistant U.S. Attorney Ryan Ellison and Special Agent in Charge Justin A. Garris of the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s Albuquerque Field Office made the announcement today. The Farmington Resident Agency of the FBI’s Albuquerque Field Office investigated this case with assistance from the Navajo Police Department and Navajo Department of Criminal Investigations. Assistant U.S. Attorney Amy Mondragon is prosecuting the case. Updated November 4, 2026 Topic Indian Country Law and Justice Components Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - New Mexico Press Release Number: 26-300

title: Western District of Oklahoma Civil Division Chief Honored with Prestigious Department of Justice Award
body: Press Release Western District of Oklahoma Civil Division Chief Honored with Prestigious Department of Justice Award Wednesday, November 4, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Oklahoma OKLAHOMA CITY – Scott Maule, Civil Division Chief for the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Western District of Oklahoma, has been nationally recognized for excellence in leadership and management by the Executive Office for the United States Attorneys (EOUSA), announced U.S. Attorney Robert J. Troester. Maule was formally recognized during the 2026 Director’s Awards ceremony on October 28, 2026, held at the Department of Justice in Washington D.C., where he received the Director’s Award for Excellence in a Managerial or Supervisory Role, an honor recognizing outstanding leadership, management, and service within the Department of Justice. Maule was one of just seven managers selected from U.S. Attorney’s Offices across the country to receive the award. Civil Division Chief Scott Maule receives the Director’s Award for Excellence in a Managerial or Supervisory Role. Pictured from left to right are Acting Deputy Attorney General Trent McCotter, Scott Maule, EOUSA Director Francey Hakes, and U.S. Attorney Robert J. Troester. “Scott is an exceptional leader whose dedication, professionalism, intellect, and commitment to public service make our office stronger every day,” said U.S. Attorney Robert J. Troester. “His ability to lead by example and navigate complex legal matters reflects the best of the Department of Justice. The people of the Western District of Oklahoma are well served by Civil Chief Scott Maule.” Maule is a 19-year veteran of the U.S. Attorney’s Office and has served as Chief of the Civil Division since 2019. He has also served as the healthcare fraud coordinator, civil rights coordinator, and the discovery coordinator for the Civil Division. From 2021-2026, Maule was selected to serve on a national Civil Chief’s Working Group where he was at the forefront of addressing the most difficult legal and policy issues facing the Department of Justice.  From 2021-2026, he also served as a member of a national eLitigation Working Group helping lead the Department’s efforts to prepare for and address the ever-emerging technical, policy, and practice issues involving eLitigation. Over his 19-year career, Maule has represented the United States and its agencies, officials, employees, and agents in a wide range of both affirmative and defensive cases at the trial and appellate level in federal and state courts. Maule received his Bachelor of Arts degree from the University of the South (Sewanee) in 1999, and his J.D. from the William & Mary Law School in 2002. The award was presented by the Director of EOUSA.  EOUSA provides oversight, general executive assistance, and direction to the 94 United States Attorneys’ offices around the country. For more information on EOUSA and its mission, visit http://www.justice.gov/usao . Updated November 4, 2026 Component USAO - Oklahoma, Western

title: Convictions through Guilty Pleas and Sentencings in Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) Prosecutions (October 26 through October 30, 2026)
body: Press Release Convictions through Guilty Pleas and Sentencings in Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) Prosecutions (October 26 through October 30, 2026) Wednesday, November 4, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Puerto Rico SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico – The United States Attorney’s Office for the District of Puerto Rico, Héctor Ramírez-Carbó, Acting United States Attorney, in conjunction with our partner agencies in the Homeland Security Task Force (“HSTF”) announce the following prosecutorial results for the week of October 26 through October 30, 2026. The HSTF is a permanent, interagency law enforcement task force created by executive order to combat transnational criminal organizations—including cartels, trafficking networks, and foreign terrorist organizations. Convictions through Guilty Pleas: On October 27, 2026, Jackson L. Nieves-Mercado pleaded guilty to Counts One and Three of the Indictment in Criminal Case No. 26-236 (MAJ). According to the Indictment, the defendant was charged with possession with intent to distribute controlled substances and the possession of a firearm in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime. Defendant was arrested on May 30, 2026. The court set defendant’s sentencing date for January 27, 2027. AUSA María Isabel López Aponte is in charge of the prosecution of the case. On October 28, 2026, siblings Alvin and Alder Lara-Martínez pleaded guilty to violating 18 U.S.C. § 1512(c)(1) in Criminal Case 25-424 (MAJ).  According to the indictment, the defendants were charged with conspiracy to destroy, alter, or conceal evidence.  Defendants were arrested on November 10, 2025. The court set defendants’ sentencing date for February 2, 2027. SAUSA Cody A. McKinney is in charge of the prosecution of the case. Sentencings: On October 29, 2026, Estefanny D. Parra-Rosa was sentenced by United States District Court Silvia Carreño Coll to one year probation for conspiracy to possess with intent to distribute controlled substances. According to court documents, defendant was indicted on June 10, 2025, in Criminal Case 25-272 (SCC) and pleaded guilty on July 29, 2026. AUSAs Laura Díaz-González and Andrés Orr in charge of the prosecution of the case. On October 30, 2026, Johan Tirado-Agueda was sentenced by United States District Court Chief Judge Raúl M. Arias-Marxuach to 70 months of imprisonment and one year of supervised release for drug-trafficking offenses. According to court documents, the defendant was originally indicted on March 30, 2023, and a superseding indictment was filed on December 4, 2025, in Criminal Case 23-125 (RAM), and the defendant pleaded guilty on February 24, 2026. AUSAs Antonio López and Antonio Pérez are in charge of the prosecution of the case. These prosecutions are part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF San Juan comprises agents and officers from the following federal partners: FBI, ICE-HSI, CBP (OFO, AMO and Border Patrol), the U.S. Marshals Service for Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands, DEA, ATF, IRS, U.S. Coast Guard, U.S. Coast Guard Investigative Service, U.S. Postal Inspection Service, the Department of State, and the U.S. Secret Service, the Puerto Rico/U.S. Virgin Islands HIDTA, TSA, FAA, and the U.S. Attorney’s Offices for the Districts of Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands. The HSTF also has the following state and local law enforcement partners as participating agencies: the Puerto Rico Police Department; the San Juan, Carolina, Guaynabo, Barceloneta, and Ponce Municipal Police Departments, the Puerto Rico National Guard – Counter Drug Program; the Puerto Rico Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation; the Puerto Rico Internal Revenue Service (Hacienda); the Puerto Rico Port Authority; and the Virgin Islands Police Department. ### Updated November 4, 2026 Topics Homeland Security Task Force Drug Trafficking Firearms Offenses Immigration Violent Crime Components Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - Puerto Rico U.S. Marshals Service Press Release Number: 2026-118

title: Midwest City Man Pleads Guilty after Making Threat Against the President
body: Press Release Midwest City Man Pleads Guilty after Making Threat Against the President Wednesday, November 4, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Oklahoma OKLAHOMA CITY – HOWARD RAYMOND GIMMEY , 47, of Midwest City, Oklahoma, has pleaded guilty to communicating a threat in interstate commerce, announced U.S. Attorney Robert J. Troester. According to public records, on May 5, 2026, Gimmey posted a message on social media stating, “I’m going to kill the President….” Court records allege that Gimmey posted the statement online, knowing that the communication would be viewed as a threat by others. On October 6, 2026, a federal grand jury charged Gimmey with communicating a threat. Gimmey pleaded guilty on November 3, 2026, and admitted he made a comment online threatening to kill the President. At sentencing, Gimmey faces up to five years in federal prison, and a fine of up to $250,000. This case is the result of an investigation by FBI Oklahoma City’s Joint Terrorism Task Force, the United States Secret Service, and the Midwest City Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorney Matt Dillon is prosecuting the case. This case is part of the nationwide National Security Presidential Memorandum 7 initiative, which is a White House directed, interagency effort to integrate federal, state, and local partners in protecting First Amendment rights while targeting individuals and organizations engaged in political violence. Reference is made to public filings for additional information. Updated November 4, 2026 Component USAO - Oklahoma, Western

title: Chinese National Admits Nationwide Gift Card Fraud
body: Press Release Chinese National Admits Nationwide Gift Card Fraud Wednesday, November 4, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Missouri ST. LOUIS – A Chinese national pleaded guilty Wednesday and admitted participating in a nationwide scam involving gift cards. Liang Xiong, 39, pleaded guilty in U.S. District Court in St. Louis to one count of possession of 15 or more unauthorized access devices. From Feb. 24, 2026, through at least March 11, 2026, Xiong stole gift cards from retailers throughout the United States, according to his plea agreement.  Xiong removed the strip concealing the serial number on the gift cards and recorded that number before placing the compromised gift cards back on display racks in stores in Colorado, Iowa and Missouri.  Once the gift cards were purchased and activated, Xiong and others intended to steal the funds on the card by using the serial number that they’d recorded. Xiong admitted stealing 15 Amazon gift cards on March 10, 2026, from a store in O’Fallon, Missouri.  The next day, he placed 16 previously stolen Apple gift cards in a display in a store in St. Charles.  He was arrested that day by the St. Charles Police Department with 134 compromised gift cards from three retailers in his vehicle.  The total value of the cards would have been $58,300 had the cards been purchased and activated by paying customers. All the gift cards in this case were recovered prior to any customers purchasing them, Xiong’s plea agreement says. Court documents indicate Xiong entered the country illegally through Mexico and has a pending asylum claim. U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement’s Homeland Security Investigations recommends looking out for signs that gift cards have been altered or counterfeited. Xiong is scheduled to be sentenced on Feb. 10, 2027. The charge carries a potential penalty of up to 10 years in prison, a fine of up to $250,000 or both prison and a fine. He will also likely be deported upon his release from prison. The case was investigated by HSI and the St. Charles Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorney Karin Schute is prosecuting the case. Contact Robert Patrick, Public Affairs Officer, robert.patrick@usdoj.gov. Updated November 4, 2026 Topic Financial Fraud Component USAO - Missouri, Eastern

title: HSTF Investigation Leads to Mexican National Being Sentenced to Prison for Drug Conspiracy
body: Press Release HSTF Investigation Leads to Mexican National Being Sentenced to Prison for Drug Conspiracy Wednesday, November 4, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Arizona TUCSON, Ariz. – Sebastian Higuera-Fuentes, 23, of Nogales, Sonora, Mexico, was sentenced on Oct. 27, by United States District Judge Raner C. Collins to 60 months in prison, followed by four years of supervised release. Higuera-Fuentes previously pleaded guilty to Conspiracy to Distribute Methamphetamine. As part of the conspiracy, Higuera-Fuentes was involved in the distribution of approximately 20 kilograms of pure methamphetamine. Higuera-Fuentes acted as a leader in the conspiracy, negotiating pricing, arranging meeting times and locations, and directing his co-conspirators to deliver the drugs. As a direct result of law enforcement’s efforts in this case, the methamphetamine never made it into Arizona communities. This prosecution is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. This HSTF Tucson investigation involved agents and officers from the Drug Enforcement Administration in Detroit, Michigan and Tucson, Arizona, Homeland Security Investigations, Federal Bureau of Investigation, Immigration and Customs Enforcement, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, United States Marshals Service, Internal Revenue Service-Criminal Investigation, ICE Enforcement and Removal Operations, United States Customs and Border Protection, United States Border Patrol, United States Postal Inspection Service, United States Secret Service, and the Bureau of Land Management. The prosecution is being by the United States Attorney’s Office for the District of Arizona. Assistant U.S. Attorney David Petermann, District of Arizona, Tucson, handled the prosecution. title: Morgan Lake Man Sentenced for Assaulting a Police Officer
body: Press Release Morgan Lake Man Sentenced for Assaulting a Police Officer Wednesday, November 4, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of New Mexico ALBUQUERQUE – A Morgan Lake man was sentenced to 17 days in custody for striking and injuring a Navajo Nation Police officer with his car. According to court documents, on September 28, 2025, officers from the Navajo Nation Police Department responded to a report of a suspected drunk driver traveling at a high rate of speed and throwing containers from his vehicle. Officers located Kendall Benally , 43, an enrolled member of the Navajo Nation, sitting behind the wheel of a van near Morgan Lake. Benally , who had been convicted twice previously of driving while intoxicated, refused repeated commands to exit the vehicle. When officers deployed pepper spray, Benally accelerated, striking an officer and a civilian and pinning them between his vehicle and a police cruiser before fleeing the scene. The officer suffered injuries to his elbow, knee and hip that required hospital treatment, while the civilian reported pain and injuries to multiple parts of his body. Benally was located and arrested later that morning. A subsequent breath alcohol test registered a blood alcohol concentration of 0.11. Benally admitted to investigators that he had consumed six beers and a double shot of liquor before driving. Benally pleaded guilty to assault with intent to commit a felony. Upon his release from prison, Benally will be subject to two years of supervised release. First Assistant U.S. Attorney Ryan Ellison and Special Agent in Charge Justin A. Garris of the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s Albuquerque Field Office made the announcement today. The Farmington Resident Agency of the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s Albuquerque Field Office investigated this case with assistance from the Navajo Nation Police Department and Navajo Department of Criminal Investigations. Assistant U.S. Attorney Jack E. Burkhead is prosecuting the case. Updated November 4, 2026 Topic Indian Country Law and Justice Components Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - New Mexico Press Release Number: 26-301

title: Los Angeles Woman Charged for $18M COVID-19 Relief Fraud Scheme
body: Press Release Los Angeles Woman Charged for $18M COVID-19 Relief Fraud Scheme Wednesday, November 4, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs A federal grand jury in the Central District of California returned an indictment yesterday charging Marisela Nuno, 53, of Los Angeles, California, with an $18 million scheme to defraud the Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) and the Economic Injury Disaster Loan (EIDL) program, federal stimulus programs authorized as part of the Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic Security (CARES) Act. According to court documents, the defendant allegedly obtained funds under the PPP and EIDL program by submitting false and fraudulent loan applications that collectively sought over $15.7 million in PPP funds and over $2.6 million in EIDL funds. The defendant is alleged to have submitted applications on behalf of businesses and entities she purportedly owned, knowing that the applications contained materially false statements and misrepresentations concerning, among other things, the purported entities’ number of employees, average monthly payroll, gross revenues, and eligibility for funding. The defendant also is alleged to have submitted materially false supporting tax documentation with the applications. The defendant then allegedly used the loan funds for purposes not authorized by the PPP or the EIDL program, including for the purchase of private property, business startup costs, and payments to family members. Nuno is charged with three counts of wire fraud and one count of money laundering. If convicted, she faces a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison on each count of wire fraud, and 10 years in prison on the count of money laundering. Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division (Fraud Division); Special Agent in Charge Robert Molvar of the FBI’s Criminal Division; Special Agent in Charge Darren Lian of the Internal Revenue Service, Criminal Investigation Division (IRS CI) Los Angeles Field Office, Special Agent in Charge Timothy Larson of the U.S. Small Business Administration Office of Inspector General (SBA OIG) made the announcement. The FBI Los Angeles Field Office, IRS CI, and SBA OIG investigated the case. Trial Attorney Ariel Glasner of the Fraud Division’s Public Trust and Financial Integrity Section and Trial Attorney Edward Emokpae of the Criminal Division’s White Collar and Corporate Enforcement Section are prosecuting the case. On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the Fraud Division. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. An indictment is merely an allegation, and all defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. Updated November 4, 2026 Topic Fraud Component National Fraud Enforcement Division Press Release Number: 26-1316

title: Tallahassee Accomplices Sentenced for Mail Theft Conspiracy
body: Press Release Tallahassee Accomplices Sentenced for Mail Theft Conspiracy Wednesday, November 4, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Florida Tallahassee, Florida –Christy Cody Holgate, 49, and Kim Demetrius Benson, 53, both of Tallahassee, Florida, have been sentenced in federal court after pleading guilty to conspiracy to commit mail theft, and multiple counts of mail theft. Holgate was sentenced to over three and a half years in federal prison. Benson was sentenced to two years’ imprisonment. The sentences were announced by John P. Heekin, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Florida. U.S. Attorney Heekin said: “These defendants sought to enrich themselves by stealing the mail, but now they’ll see the inside of a federal prison cell. My office is committed to aggressively prosecuting anyone who tampers with, steals, or diverts the U.S. Mail to ensure our citizens can continue to rely upon the U.S. Postal Service to quickly, safely, and securely deliver the mail.” Court documents reflect that between August 5, 2025, and December 5, 2025, the defendants broke into multiple apartment complex mailboxes through use of United States Postal Service (USPS) mail key that permitted access to the mail of complex residents. Through investigation, the U.S. Postal Inspection Service and Tallahassee Police Department documented multiple thefts of hundreds of pieces of mail. They also obtained video surveillance which captured the break-ins. Upon their arrest in December 2025, the two were found in a vehicle containing bags of stolen mail items along with stolen debit and credit cards, as well as a USPS mail key. Together, the defendants conspired to steal U.S. Mail, which, according to a confession by Holgate, was then sold to another individual for money to purchase illegal drugs. This case was jointly investigated by the Tallahassee Police Department and the United States Postal Inspection Service. The case was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Eric K. Mountin. title: Western District of Arkansas Staff Honored by  Attorney General Todd Blanche at 2026 Director’s Awards
body: Press Release Western District of Arkansas Staff Honored by  Attorney General Todd Blanche at 2026 Director’s Awards Wednesday, November 4, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Arkansas FORT SMITH – Assistant United States Attorney Dustin Roberts and Assistant United States Attorney Kevin Eaton of the United States Attorney’s Office for the Western District of Arkansas were among 183 Department of Justice employees recognized by Attorney General Todd Blanche and Executive Office for U.S. Attorneys (EOUSA) Director Francey Hakes at the 2026 Director’s Awards Ceremony held October 28 in the Great Hall of the Robert F. Kennedy Department of Justice Building in Washington, D.C. The awards recognize outstanding achievements by employees of the United States Attorney’s Offices. “I am incredibly proud of Assistant United States Attorneys Dustin Roberts and Kevin Eaton. Their dedication, integrity, and genuine commitment to protecting the people of the Western District of Arkansas shine through in everything they do,” said Kevin R. Holmes, United States Attorney for the Western District of Arkansas. “This recognition from the Attorney General is a truly deserved honor, and I’m grateful to serve alongside them.” Excellence in a Managerial Role This award recognizes an employee who has accomplished superior managerial and supervisory achievements over at least the last three years. In 2025, Western Arkansas experienced a 7 year high in prosecutions, with Assistant United States Attorney Dustin Roberts serving as Criminal Chief over 13 AUSAs, often serving as second chair in trials. In addition to his supervisory duties, he maintained a full load of criminal cases as lead prosecutor, to include United States vs. Joshua Duggar, which drew national attention. Excellence as an Appellate Assistant United States Attorney This award recognizes AUSAs who perform appellate work for their USAO and who have distinguished themselves through the outstanding performance of their duties. In 2025 Assistant United States Attorney Kevin Eaton handled several high-profile cases, four of which he argued at the Eighth Circuit within a ten-month period. The oral arguments involved defending the constitutionality of the federal ban on machineguns, resisting a defendant’s attempts to import the requirements of Apprendi into supervised release hearings, and defending a denial of a suppression motion raising unique issues involving the interplay between Arkansas law and the Fourth Amendment. Please join us in congratulating these award recipients on their well-earned honors. Their accomplishments demonstrate a strong commitment to excellence in public service and reflect the dedication of the entire Western District of Arkansas team. body: Press Release Georgia Man Pleads Guilty to Fatal Shooting and Carjacking Wednesday, November 4, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of New Mexico ALBUQUERQUE – A Georgia man pleaded guilty to fatally shooting a woman as she pumped gas at an Acoma Pueblo travel center before stealing her vehicle and fleeing from law enforcement. According to court documents, on February 1, 2025, Jaquari Hezakiyah Porter , 26, approached Jane Doe as she was pumping gas at the Sky City Travel Center in Acoma, New Mexico. Porter shot the victim twice, killing her, and stole her vehicle before fleeing toward Grants. Porter subsequently encountered officers from the Cibola County Sheriff's Office and Grants Police Department. He attempted to flee and fired at officers, who returned fire, striking Porter twice before apprehending him and taking him into custody. Porter pleaded guilty to carjacking resulting in death and using and carrying a firearm during and in relation to a crime of violence. At sentencing Porter faces up to life in prison. title: Last of Three Defendants Sentenced to 16 Years in Prison for Role in Armed Carjackings
body: Press Release Last of Three Defendants Sentenced to 16 Years in Prison for Role in Armed Carjackings Wednesday, November 4, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Ohio CLEVELAND – A 22-year-old man has been sentenced to prison for his role during violent carjackings in Cleveland in July 2025. Tayveonn Elliott, of Cleveland, was sentenced to 192 months (16 years) in prison and five years of supervised released by U.S. District Judge Patricia A. Gaughan after pleading guilty to: •    Carjacking •    Using or Carrying and Brandishing a Firearm During a Crime of Violence Judge Gaughan also ordered him to pay $25,199.81 in restitution, jointly and severally with co-defendants Mickey Hodge, 23, and Tye Campbell, 20, both of Cleveland. Hodge is currently serving a 20-year prison sentence, and Campbell was sentenced to 12 and a half years in prison. According to court documents, on July 16, 2025, three victims were carjacked by a coordinated group of armed assailants, later identified as Hodge, Elliott, and Campbell. The day before the carjackings, a food delivery service employee left his Honda Civic briefly to deliver food to a residence. But when he returned, his car was gone. The next morning at 4 a.m., the defendants threatened a valet at a downtown hotel and demanded the keys to vehicles she had parked. In fear of her life, she complied and the suspects took a Nissan Altima, while a third co-conspirator drove away in the Honda stolen from the delivery service driver. At about 7:30 a.m. the same morning, a woman sitting in her Toyota RAV4 was carjacked at gunpoint in a gym parking lot. Also fearing for her life, she gave the suspects the car keys and they drove off. Later, at about 6 p.m., a third victim was threatened at gunpoint, and he gave the suspects the keys to his Ford Explorer. About four hours later, law enforcement located the Honda Civic and activated lights to initiate a traffic stop. However, the Honda sped away and crashed into two other vehicles at an intersection.  Several suspects, including Hodge and Elliott, got out of the car  and fled on foot but were apprehended. Campbell was arrested on a later date. The investigation was conducted by the FBI Cleveland Division and the Cleveland Division of Police. Assistant United States Attorney Scott Zarzycki led the prosecution for the Northern District of Ohio. title: Illegal Alien Sentenced in D.C. to 97 Months for Brokering Fentanyl and Cocaine Deals From Texas Prison
body: Press Release Illegal Alien Sentenced in D.C. to 97 Months for Brokering Fentanyl and Cocaine Deals From Texas Prison Wednesday, November 4, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Columbia WASHINGTON – Gilberto Paz Madrid, 41, a citizen of Mexico, was sentenced today in U.S. District Court to 97 months in federal prison for his role as a broker in a fentanyl and cocaine conspiracy while he was incarcerated in Texas for a previous heroin trafficking offense, announced U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro. “This illegal alien was already behind bars for trafficking heroin, yet he used a smuggled cellphone to broker fentanyl and cocaine deals aimed at D.C. streets,” said U.S. Attorney Pirro. “Prison walls will not stop us from pursuing traffickers who endanger our communities, and when he finishes his sentence, he will face deportation.” Paz Madrid, aka “Taco,” pleaded guilty on July 2 before Judge Timothy J. Kelly to conspiracy to distribute 40 grams or more of fentanyl and 500 grams or more of cocaine. The 97-month prison term will be served after he completes a 10-year sentence for heroin trafficking out of the Eastern District of Virginia. Madrid faces deportation after serving his time in federal prison. According to court documents, Paz Madrid was incarcerated and serving a 120-month sentence at FCI Beaumont in Texas in February 2024 when an individual sent a WhatsApp message to a contraband cellphone Paz Madrid was using in prison. The individual claimed to have received Paz Madrid’s number from a mutual acquaintance and explained that he was hoping Paz Madrid could broker an introduction to drug customers in the United States. In a later WhatsApp call, the individual stated that they could distribute both “F” (meaning fentanyl) and “blanco” (meaning cocaine). During a subsequent call between the two, Paz Madrid added co-defendant Jermaine Horne to the conversation. Horne asked the price for a kilo of cocaine, which the individual indicated would be between $17,000 and $18,000. Paz Madrid also advised that individual that Horne and his associates could assist the individual with the “F” and “cuadros” (meaning fentanyl and kilograms, respectively). On March 6, 2024, another person reached out to Horne via telephone. The person indicated that he was a courier working for the individual. The person asked, “So what you need?” Horne replied, “He told you right?  He was saying you were bringing four.” The person asked, “four or five?”  Horne said, “I thought he said four but five, that’s cool.” The person clarified that they were told to deliver fentanyl. Horne responded that he was expecting “up” (meaning cocaine).  The person ended that call by telling Horne that they needed to make sure everyone was on the same page and would call Horne back. Following the call with Horne, the person called Paz Madrid. The two discussed the type of drug to be delivered to Horne. Paz Madrid indicated it would be the “blanco” (meaning cocaine). The person indicated that he could deliver four kilograms to Horne. The person later spoke again with Horne. Horne made clear that he wanted four kilograms of cocaine and one kilogram of fentanyl.  The two made plans to meet the following week. The narcotics were slated to be delivered March 14, 2024, to Horne in the District. However, Horne apparently saw surveillance vehicles in the area, and he did not enter the pre-arranged location to purchase the narcotics. In later conversations, Horne later told Paz Madrid that he did not like the location because it was near a police station, a message that Paz Madrid conveyed to the would-be supplier. Horne pleaded guilty on July 28 to conspiracy to distribute 40 grams or more of fentanyl and 500 grams or more of cocaine. Sentencing is pending. This investigation was conducted by the FBI Washington Field Office with valuable assistance from the White County (Arkansas) Sheriff’s Office, Nash County (North Carolina) Sheriff’s Office, the Bureau of Prisons Office of Special Investigations, and the Metropolitan Police Department. The matter is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Nihar Mohanty of the Violent Crime and Narcotics Trafficking Section. 24cr139 Updated November 4, 2026 Topic Drug Trafficking Components Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) Federal Bureau of Prisons (BOP) USAO - District of Columbia

title: Lehigh Acres Man Pleads Guilty to Wire Fraud and Illegal Monetary Transactions
body: Press Release Lehigh Acres Man Pleads Guilty to Wire Fraud and Illegal Monetary Transactions Wednesday, November 4, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Middle District of Florida Fort Myers, Florida – Thakur Sukhdeo (40, Lehigh Acres) has pleaded guilty to two counts of wire fraud and two counts of illegal monetary transactions related to COVID relief. He faces a maximum penalty of 20 years in federal prison for each wire fraud count, and up to 10 years’ imprisonment for each illegal monetary transaction count. Sukhdeo has also agreed to forfeit $413,900, which are the proceeds of the criminal offense. U.S. Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe made the announcement. According to court records, during the COVID pandemic, the United States Small Business Administration (SBA) offered loans to small businesses under the Economic Injury Disaster Loan (EIDL). Beginning around April 2021, Sukhdeo engaged in a scheme to fraudulently obtain $413,900 by applying for an EIDL loan from the SBA using false pretenses and representations. To secure the loan, Sukhdeo submitted loan paperwork to the SBA claiming that he owned a handyman business that made $206,998 in 2019. However, bank records revealed the business made $19,843.50 that year. As part of the loan, Sukhdeo promised to only use the EIDL funds on business expenses. After applying for the loan, on March 24, 2022, the SBA deposited $413,900 into Sukhdeo’s personal bank account. The following day, Sukhdeo created a business account and transferred the entirety of the EIDL funds to that account. Shortly thereafter, Sukhdeo utilized the EIDL funds to purchase a luxury vehicle for $68,984.61 and a truck for $93,994.42. Sukhdeo also made numerous cash withdrawals of the EIDL funds in the amount of $172,505, as well as other personal purchases. Within one year, Sukhdeo had spent all of the EIDL funds. The FBI subsequently seized both of Sukhdeo’s vehicles and on January 13, 2025, the court ordered the civil forfeiture of both vehicles. This case was investigated by FBI. It is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Matthew Redavid. The forfeiture is being handled by Assistant United States Attorney Suzanne C. Nebesky. title: Rockford Man Sentenced to More Than 15 Years in Federal Prison for Trafficking Cocaine
body: Press Release Rockford Man Sentenced to More Than 15 Years in Federal Prison for Trafficking Cocaine Wednesday, November 4, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Illinois A Rockford man has been sentenced to more than fifteen years in federal prison for trafficking cocaine and illegally possessing a loaded firearm. WILLIAM SPEARS was arrested in June 2024 following a 4-month narcotics investigation.  At the time of his arrest, Spears was in possession of three and a half grams of cocaine, which he had been planning to sell to another person.  Following his arrest, law enforcement searched Spears’s residence and a storage unit he rented and discovered approximately 700 grams of cocaine, $17,000 in cash, and a loaded handgun. Spears, 68, pleaded guilty earlier this year to possession with intent to distribute more than 500 grams of cocaine and possession of a firearm by a prohibited person. As a previously convicted felon, Spears was prohibited from possessing firearms.  On Oct. 30, 2026, U.S. District Judge Iain D. Johnston sentenced Spears to 15 years and eight months in federal prison. The sentence was announced by Andrew S. Boutros, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Illinois, and Christopher Amon, Special Agent in Charge of the Chicago Division of the U.S. Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives. The Winnebago County, Ill. Sheriff’s Office assisted in the investigation. “Defendant’s actions significantly contributed to the drug problem plaguing the Rockford community,” Assistant U.S. Attorney Andrew M. Rosati argued in the government’s sentencing memorandum.  “A significant sentence is necessary to protect the public and the community from defendant’s continued drug trafficking activities.” Updated November 4, 2026 Topics Drug Trafficking Firearms Offenses Violent Crime Components Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) USAO - Illinois, Northern

title: Bergen County Man Sentenced to 20 Years’ Imprisonment for Receipt and Possession of Child Pornography
body: Press Release Bergen County Man Sentenced to 20 Years’ Imprisonment for Receipt and Possession of Child Pornography Wednesday, November 4, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of New Jersey NEWARK, N.J. – A Bergen County, New Jersey man was sentenced to 20 years’ imprisonment for receipt and possession of multiple images of child sexual abuse, U.S. Attorney Robert Frazer announced. Corey Hipscher, 55, of Lodi, New Jersey previously pleaded guilty yesterday before U.S. district Judge Wiliam J. Martini in Newark federal court to an Information charging him with receipt and possession of child pornography. According to documents filed in this case and statements made in court: From 2020 to August 2023, Hipscher communicated with a minor victim located outside of the United States using a social media platform. Hipscher encouraged the minor victim to send Hipscher images and videos of the minor victim engaging in sexually explicit conduct. Hipscher also began an online romantic relationship with the minor victim’s mother which he used to arrange for the minor victim and the minor victim’s family to visit him in New Jersey. During the visit, he sexually assaulted the minor victim and took sexually explicit photos of the minor victim and the minor victim’s sibling. In addition to the prison term, Judge Martini sentenced Hipscher to 15 years of supervised release. U.S. Attorney Frazer credited FBI Newark’s Child Exploitation and Human Trafficking Task Force, under the direction of Special Agent in Charge Stefanie Roddy in Newark, with the investigation leading to the charges. U.S. Attorney Frazer also thanked the Lodi Police Department and the Bergen County Prosecutor’s Office. This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and the Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS) in the Justice Department’s Criminal Division, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.projectsafechildhood.gov U.S. Attorney Frazer has announced proactive steps to connect with New Jersey’s families and communities, bringing training opportunities and resources through direct outreach. Organizations and community members interested in arranging prevention programming or learning more about available resources can contact the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of New Jersey at USANJ.CommunityOutreach@usdoj.gov . Moreover, prevention resources are available through the Department of Justice's Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section Prevention webpage and the Department of Homeland Security’s Know2Protect Campaign. The government is represented by Assistant U.S. Attorney Sean Nadel of the Cybercrime Unit in Newark. ### Defense counsel: Anthony Pope, Esq. Updated November 4, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Component USAO - New Jersey Press Release Number: 26-242

title: Illegal Alien from the Dominican Republic Pleads Guilty to SNAP Fraud and MassHealth Benefit Fraud
body: Press Release Illegal Alien from the Dominican Republic Pleads Guilty to SNAP Fraud and MassHealth Benefit Fraud Wednesday, November 4, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Massachusetts Defendant stole over $57,000 in MassHealth benefits and over $15,000 in SNAP benefits BOSTON – A Dominican man unlawfully residing in Dorchester pleaded guilty in federal court in Boston to Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits fraud and false writing relating health care matters. Danis Piron Lara, 51, pleaded guilty to unlawfully obtaining SNAP Benefits and making a false writing relating to health care matters. U.S. Senior District Court Judge F. Dennis Saylor scheduled sentencing for Jan. 27, 2026. Piron Lara was charged in March 2026 . Piron Lara obtained various Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles identifications using the name and other information of an American citizen from Puerto Rico. Specifically, beginning in 2005, Piron Lara used the victim’s identity to obtain MassHealth benefits, receiving benefits he was not entitled to in 2005, 2006, 2009 through 2014, 2016, and 2018 through March 2026. In total, he received $57,289.26 in MassHealth benefits under the victim’s identity. Between April 2021 and March 2026, Piron Lara posing as the victim received $15,186 in SNAP benefits. The charge of unlawfully obtaining SNAP benefits provides for a sentence of up to 20 years in prison, three years of supervised release and a fine of $250,000. The charge of making false statements relating to a health care program provides for a sentence of up to five years in prison, one year of supervised release and a fine of $250,000. Sentences are imposed by a federal district court judge based upon the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and statutes which govern the determination of a sentence in a criminal case. Sentences are imposed by a federal district court judge based upon the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and statutes which govern the determination of a sentence in a criminal case. On March 26, 2026 , United States Attorney Leah B. Foley announced the creation of the Benefit & Voter Fraud Team, a district-wide initiative established in response to the rampant fraud being uncovered across Massachusetts. Members of the public are encouraged to report suspected benefit fraud in Massachusetts by calling 1-855-SCAM-MA-1 (855-722-6621). title: Morriston Man Pleads Guilty to Federal Child Exploitation Crimes
body: Press Release Morriston Man Pleads Guilty to Federal Child Exploitation Crimes Wednesday, November 4, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Florida Gainesville, Florida – Bryan Cardozo-Mendieta, 21, of Morriston, Florida, pleaded guilty in federal court to one count of attempted enticement of a minor and one count of possession of child pornography. The plea was announced by John P. Heekin, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Florida. U.S. Attorney Heekin said: “I am proud that my office was able to successfully prosecute this sick individual for these heinous crimes, and we remain committed to aggressively pursuing predators like him to ensure our kids are kept safe from sexual exploitation and victimization.” Court documents reflect that on November 17, 2025, the defendant was communicating with an individual he believed to be a minor. The defendant travelled from Levy County to Kissimmee, Florida, with the intention of engaging in sexual activity with the child. On or about November 8, 2025, the defendant also inappropriately touched a different child. When the defendant was arrested for these offenses, his cell phone contained over 500 images of child sexual abuse material. Cardozo faces a mandatory minimum sentence of ten years’ imprisonment, and up to a maximum of life imprisonment. The case involved a joint investigation by the Homeland Security Investigations and the Levy County Sheriff’s Office. Assistant United States Attorney Adam Hapner is prosecuting the case. Sentencing is scheduled for January 26, 2027, at 10:30 a.m. at the United States Courthouse in Gainesville before Chief United States District Judge Allen C. Winsor. This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. title: Two Men Plead Guilty to Interstate Armed Robbery of a Londonderry Warehouse
body: Press Release Two Men Plead Guilty to Interstate Armed Robbery of a Londonderry Warehouse Wednesday, November 4, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of New Hampshire Av Harris (603) 230-2576 usanh.media@usdoj.gov CONCORD – Two men pleaded guilty in federal court for conspiring to interfere with commerce by robbery, U.S. Attorney Erin Creegan announces. Nasaiah Johnson, 25, recently of Baltimore, Maryland, and Xiao Yu, 28, an illegal alien from China recently living in New Jersey, pleaded guilty before U.S. District Court Judge Steven McAuliffe earlier today. Johnson’s sentencing is set for February 16, 2027. Yu’s sentencing is set for February 23, 2027. According to the court documents and statements made in court, Johnson and Yu, along with four co-conspirators, traveled from New York to New England, for the purpose of robbing a local business. Yu rented a box truck from a rental agency in Medford, Massachusetts, and purchased supplies from a hardware store there. The co-conspirators then traveled to a business in Londonderry, New Hampshire. Five individuals, including Johnson, entered the business where they threatened an employee with what appeared to be a firearm and restrained the victim. The men then proceeded to steal merchandise and goods from the business, placing those items into the box truck, which was driven by Yu. Yu left in the box truck, while the other co-conspirators fled the scene in a sedan and returned to New York. The charge of conspiracy to interfere with commerce by robbery carries a maximum prison term of 20 years, a maximum fine of $250,000, and not more than 3 years of supervised release. Sentences are imposed by a federal district court judge based upon the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and statutes which govern the determination of a sentence in a criminal case. The Federal Bureau of Investigation led this investigation. The Londonderry Police Department, New Hampshire State Police, Massachusetts State Police, and New York Police Department provided valuable assistance. Assistant U.S. Attorney Matthew Vicinanzo is prosecuting the case.
