title: Six Sentenced to Combined 37 Years in Federal Prison for Drug Trafficking
body: Press Release Six Sentenced to Combined 37 Years in Federal Prison for Drug Trafficking Wednesday, November 4, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of West Virginia MARTINSBURG, WEST VIRGINIA – Six drug traffickers were sentenced today to a combined 37 years in federal prison for selling fentanyl, cocaine, and methamphetamine in the Eastern Panhandle of West Virginia, announced U.S. Attorney Matthew L. Harvey. The separate cases are a part of a collaborative effort by multiple states and jurisdictions to arrest offenders and remove deadly drugs from our communities. Those sentenced are: Kenneth Robert Eversole, 48, of Keyser, West Virginia, was sentenced to 168 months in federal prison for having more than 400 grams of fentanyl in Mineral County. Eversole was a source of supply for other drug traffickers in the Keyser area, distributing large quantities of pressed fentanyl pills and methamphetamine. Investigators determined Eversole distributed hundreds of fentanyl pills and executed a search warrant at the duplex where he resided. Officers seized nearly three pounds of fentanyl, almost two pounds of methamphetamine, 150 pounds of marijuana, and a small amount of cocaine. Along with the drugs, officers seized five firearms, cash, body armor, and drug paraphernalia. Brenton Daniel Berens, 38, was sentenced to 60 months in prison and Shannon Lynn Smith, 40, was sentenced to 60 months for their roles in a drug trafficking operation selling fentanyl and cocaine in Berkeley County. Berens and Smith, both of Martinsburg, West Virginia, maintained a residence to store and package the drugs to serve as a distribution hub for the operation. Officers searched the home and seized nearly one pound of fentanyl. Investigators traced the drugs back to a Baltimore, Maryland man, Rodney Harry Augustine. Augustine was convicted for his role in this case and will be sentenced in 2027. Malachi Brian Maurice Younger, 23, was sentenced to 41 months in prison for trafficking fentanyl and cocaine in Berkeley County. Younger was selling fentanyl and cocaine in West Virginia and Maryland, crossing state lines to continue his drug operation. During a traffic stop, officers seized more than a half a pound of cocaine, more than 50 grams of fentanyl, and a quarter pound of marijuana from his vehicle. Shawn Douglas Kile, 29, of Keyser, West Virginia, was sentenced to 120 months in federal prison for distributing 50 grams or more of methamphetamine. Kile was selling methamphetamine, sometimes using his social media to communicate with customers. Investigators determined he sold a little more than 93 grams of methamphetamine in Mineral County. “These sentences reflect the commitment of our federal, state, and local law enforcement partners who work tirelessly to protect our communities. Thanks to their exceptional teamwork, these dangerous traffickers have been removed from our streets, and our community is safer as a result. But our work does not end here. My office will continue to aggressively pursue those who choose to traffic deadly drugs into West Virginia and will remain relentless in our efforts to eliminate drug networks wherever they operate,” said U.S. Attorney Matthew L. Harvey. Criminal Division Chief Lara Omps-Botteicher prosecuted the cases on behalf of the government. Investigative agencies include the Drug Enforcement Administration; the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives; the Washington County, Maryland Narcotics Task Force; the Eastern Panhandle Drug Task Force, a HIDTA-funded initiative; the Potomac Highlands Drug Task Force, a HIDTA-funded initiative; the Maryland State Police; the Hagerstown, MD Police Department; and the Washington County, MD Sheriff’s Department. The prosecution of these cases directly advances a core priority of our office’s Four Corners of Public Safety initiative: stopping the flow of illegal drugs into the Northern District of West Virginia. Drug trafficking poses a serious threat to public safety, fueling addiction, harming families, and endangering communities. By focusing on dismantling drug trafficking activity, this effort reinforces our commitment to keeping dangerous drugs off the streets and safeguarding the people of Northern District of West Virginia. To learn more about the Four Corners of Public Safety, click here . Fentanyl has been designated by President Donald Trump as a weapon of mass destruction due to its extreme lethality which poses a grave threat to public safety, even in trace amounts. This case is part of Operation Take Back America , a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime, and repel the invasion of illegal immigration. U.S. District Judge Gina M. Groh presided. Updated November 4, 2026 Topics Operation Take Back America Drug Trafficking Component USAO - West Virginia, Northern

title: Utah Minor Recovered by Law Enforcement After Oregon Man Allegedly Transported the Victim to Engage in Criminal Sexual Activity
body: Press Release Utah Minor Recovered by Law Enforcement After Oregon Man Allegedly Transported the Victim to Engage in Criminal Sexual Activity Wednesday, November 4, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs An Oregon man is now in federal custody and charged in a criminal complaint with transportation with intent to engage in criminal sexual activity after he allegedly met a Utah minor online in May 2025, drove to Utah to pick up the victim, and then transported the victim to his residence across state lines.  The minor was recovered by law enforcement at the residence on Nov. 1. “Anyone engaged in the sexual exploitation of a minor will be held accountable,” said Attorney General Todd Blanche. “Today’s arrest is the first step toward bringing the accused to justice and relieving the pain endured by the victim and her family. This Department of Justice will never stop investigating and prosecuting individuals engaged in vicious predatory behavior.” “This individual is charged with transporting a minor to another state to engage in criminal sexual activity, a minor who was missing for a year and a half until Oregon police recovered her based on information provided by the FBI,” said FBI Director Kash Patel. “According to the criminal complaint the minor was groomed on gaming platforms and engaged in acts of self-harm and sexually explicit activity. To anyone targeting and exploiting children: this FBI and our partners are coming for you. We are using every tool at our disposal to combat nihilistic violent extremism, bring offenders to justice, and protect America’s most vulnerable. I want to thank the FBI Salt Lake Field Office, the Oregon State Police, and federal prosecutors for their outstanding work on this case.” “Our priority in this case was the safe return of the minor victim,” said U.S. Attorney Melissa Holyoak for the District of Utah. “Those who allegedly exploit and prey upon the most vulnerable members of our communities will be relentlessly investigated and held accountable. I want to thank the FBI and our local law enforcement partners in Oregon for their swift efforts to safely recover the victim and for their continued partnership as we pursue justice for the victim and the victim’s family.” Adam Hunter Harmel, 39, of Huntington, Oregon, was charged in a federal complaint on Nov. 2 in the District of Utah. He had his initial appearance on the complaint on Nov. 4 at the U.S. District Courthouse in Boise, Idaho. According to court documents, beginning in or about May 2025 and continuing until Nov. 1, in the District of Utah and elsewhere, Harmel allegedly transported the minor victim with the intent to engage in sexual activity with the victim. On or about Aug. 20, 2025, FBI Salt Lake City received information that the minor victim had disappeared in May 2025. During the investigation, the FBI learned that the minor victim was allegedly groomed on gaming platforms that are commonly used by Nihilistic Violent Extremist (NVE) Groups members to solicit sexually explicit photos and maiming photos. The grooming then transitioned to other social media applications. On Nov. 1, the FBI received a tip about the possible location of the minor victim and that the victim met Harmel on a social media application in May 2025. As alleged in court documents, Harmel kept a knife under his pillow to prevent the minor victim from escaping. The case is being investigated by the FBI Salt Lake City Field Office in conjunction with the FBI Joint Terrorism Task Force. Valuable assistance was provided by the Oregon State Police. Assistant U.S. Attorney Jawayria Z. Auchter for the District of Utah and Trial Attorneys Justin Sher and James Donnelly of the National Security Division’s Counterterrorism Section are prosecuting the case. A complaint is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. Updated November 4, 2026 Topic National Security Components Office of the Attorney General Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) National Security Division (NSD) USAO - Utah Press Release Number: 26-1320

title: Raymore Woman Pleads Guilty to Tax Refund Fraud Scheme
body: Press Release Raymore Woman Pleads Guilty to Tax Refund Fraud Scheme Wednesday, November 4, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Missouri Teneika Reynolds, 50, pleaded guilty before U.S. District Judge Greg Kays, to aiding and assisting in the preparation of false tax returns. Reynolds was the owner and operator of TR Tax Service, a tax preparation business operating in Kansas City. Reynolds prepared and electronically filed returns claiming false items including Schedule C business expenses, false Forms 7202, Sick and Family Leave Credits, and fictitious Household Help income for client-taxpayers for the tax years 2019 to 2023.  This resulted in refunds larger than what her clients were entitled to receive. Reynolds assisted at least 15 individuals file at least 33 false and fraudulent income tax returns for tax years 2019 through 2023. Specifically, on Feb. 8, 2022, Reynolds aided and assisted in the filing of an IRS Form 1040, U.S. Individual Income Tax Return, with the Internal Revenue Service. On that form, Reynolds included false Sick and Family Leave credits, resulting in a fraudulent refund. Under federal statutes, Reynolds is subject to a sentence of up to three years in federal prison without parole. The maximum statutory sentence is prescribed by Congress and is provided here for informational purposes, as the sentencing of Reynolds will be determined by the court based on the advisory sentencing guidelines and other statutory factors. A sentencing hearing will be scheduled after the completion of a presentence investigation by the United States Probation Office. This case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Rudolph R. Rhodes IV.   It was investigated by Internal Revenue Service-Criminal Investigation. The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. title: Ex-Postal Worker Receives Six-and-a-Half-Year Sentence for Stealing Checks in Massive $34 Million Fraud Scheme
body: Press Release Ex-Postal Worker Receives Six-and-a-Half-Year Sentence for Stealing Checks in Massive $34 Million Fraud Scheme Wednesday, November 4, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of Indiana INDIANAPOLIS- A former United States Postal Service letter carrier, Destinee Ruffin, 29, of Indianapolis, has been sentenced to six and a half years in federal prison, followed by two years of supervised release, after pleading guilty to Conspiracy to Commit Bank Fraud and Theft of Mail. This case was brought as part of the Trump Administration’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud. According to court documents, Ruffin was employed as a letter carrier at the Bacon Station Post Office. Between April 2020 and May 2022, Ruffin used access to both incoming and outgoing mail to steal checks, which she then sold to co-conspirators. In spring 2020, as the federal government issued Economic Impact Payment (EIP) checks to taxpayers, the USPS OIG received a complaint from a Bacon Station customer who never received theirs. Additional complaints soon followed. When agents reviewed the affected addresses and matched them to delivery routes, they discovered all missing checks were assigned to the same mail carrier, Destinee Ruffin. In one example, Ruffin and McMullen exchanged 38 Cash App transactions totaling over $10,000 in payments from McMullen to Ruffin for stolen checks. Using the stolen checks, McMullen sought individuals on social media who were willing to deposit altered checks into their bank accounts. These individuals provided debit cards, PINs, or online banking credentials. McMullen altered the payee information on the stolen checks, deposited them, and later withdrew funds or demanded payment through Cash App or Zelle. In total, McMullen fraudulently negotiated 36 checks stolen from Bacon Station, worth approximately $235,632. Ruffin sold even more stolen checks to Young. Young established trusted mid-level conspirators, primarily Eric Hollis (Hollis) and Kendall Thompson (Thompson), who deposited stolen checks into various accounts and recruited/ acquired account holders. Young would also list many of the stolen checks for sale on the internet-based application titled “Telegram.” Investigators uncovered the scheme by mailing controlled Treasury checks with recorded serial numbers and tracing them back to Ruffin’s delivery route. In April 2024, officers executed a search warrant on Ruffin’s vehicle, residence, person, and electronic devices. They discovered thousands of stolen checks valued at over $20 million that Ruffin had stolen but not yet sold. Stolen mail was found in her vehicle, on shelves, in closets, on the floor, stacked in corners, and even in the bathroom. In total, Ruffin supplied Young with more than $12 million in stolen checks and provided McMullen with stolen checks worth more than $235,000. For the intended recipients, the impact was severe. One victim explained that after mailing a $1,618 check to Sheet Metal Workers Local Union No. 20 Welfare and Benefit Fund—needed to maintain her retired husband’s health insurance—she learned the payment never arrived. She discovered the theft when she appeared for a scheduled surgery and was told her insurance had been terminated, forcing the procedure to be canceled. The United States Attorney’s Office estimates that approximately 6,500 victims were affected by this widespread fraud scheme. Three of Ruffin’s co-conspirators have already been sentenced for their roles in the scheme. The final co-conspirator, John Young, is scheduled to be sentenced on December 3 rd , 2026. Defendant Charge(s) Sentence Restitution Tony McMullen, 36, Calumet Park, IL Conspiracy to commit bank fraud Two years, nine months; three years of supervised release $121,270.30 Eric Hollis, 23, Indianapolis Conspiracy to commit bank fraud One year and one day; three years of supervised release $117,275.30 Kendall Thompson, 24, Indianapolis Conspiracy to commit bank fraud Four months; three years of supervised release $9,320.05 Destinee Ruffin, 29, Indianapolis Conspiracy to commit bank fraud; theft of mail Six and a half years; Two years of supervised release $121,270.30 John Young, 24, Indianapolis Attempt and Conspiracy to commit mail fraud; three counts of Bank fraud Sentencing date scheduled for December 3, 2026 TBD “Destinee Ruffin’s crimes were not isolated acts of theft; they represented a sweeping scheme that touched thousands of households and eroded a fundamental public trust. By stealing millions of dollars’ worth of checks from the mail, Ruffin and her co-conspirators disrupted critical benefits, jeopardized family finances, and caused real harm to individuals who depended on timely delivery for essential needs,” said Tom Wheeler, United States Attorney for the Southern District of Indiana. “Today’s sentence reflects our commitment to protecting the integrity of the U.S. Postal Service and all government institutions, and to ensuring that those who exploit them for personal gain are held fully accountable.” “The Treasury Inspector General for Tax Administration (TIGTA) aggressively investigates individuals who attempt to exploit U.S Treasury refund checks meant for hard working taxpayers for their own private gain,” said TIGTA Special Agent in Charge Kelly Moening. TIGTA’s mission is to protect the integrity of our nation’s tax administration system.  We are committed to working with our law enforcement partners to ensure that those who violate federal laws are prosecuted to the fullest extent possible. The U.S. Postal Service – Office of Inspector General, the United States Postal Inspection Service, and the Treasury Inspector General for Tax Administration investigated this case. The sentences were imposed by U.S. District Court Judge Sarah Evans Barker. U.S. Attorney Wheeler thanked Assistant U.S. Attorney Adam Eakman, who prosecuted this case. On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (“Fraud Division”). The Fraud Division is investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. ### Updated November 4, 2026 Topic Fraud Components National Fraud Enforcement Division USAO - Indiana, Southern

body: Press Release Gainesville Felon Pleads Guilty to Possession of a Firearm and Ammunition Wednesday, November 4, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Florida Gainesville, Florida – Peter Guiseppe Stefani, 25, of Levy County, Florida, pleaded guilty in federal court to one count of possession of a firearm and ammunition by a convicted felon. title: Man Involved in Two Separate Shootings in Charlotte Convicted at Trial for Possession of Ammunition by a  Felon
body: Press Release Man Involved in Two Separate Shootings in Charlotte Convicted at Trial for Possession of Ammunition by a  Felon Wednesday, November 4, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of North Carolina CHARLOTTE, N.C. – A federal jury in Charlotte returned a guilty verdict against Kenneth Fuller, 43, of Charlotte, for possession of ammunition by a felon, announced Russ Ferguson, U.S. Attorney for the Western District of North Carolina. U.S. District Judge Kenneth D. Bell presided over the three-day trial. “This convicted felon shot into two businesses while employees and patrons were present,” said U.S. Attorney Russ Ferguson.  “We cannot stand idly by when people endanger innocent life. By putting people like Fuller behind bars, everyone else can go about their daily life without worrying about their safety.” “Such a careless and blatant disregard for public safety puts our entire community at risk,” said ATF Special Agent in Charge Alicia Jones. “ATF and our law enforcement partners will continue to hold reckless individuals accountable for their violent threats and dangerous behavior.” Fuller was indicted by a federal grand jury in 2026, on two counts of possession of ammunition by a convicted felon, stemming from his involvement in two separate shootings. The first shooting happened on December 20, 2024, at a Waffle House in Charlotte. Officers with the Charlotte-Mecklenburg Department (CMPD) were dispatched to the Waffle House at approximately 5:53 a.m. Upon arrival, the officers spoke with multiple witnesses and employees who explained that an individual, later identified as Fuller, claimed he paid too much and demanded a refund. Fuller then became upset and shot a handgun into the air. Fuller then returned to his vehicle, a black Maserati sedan, and drove off. Officers searched the area and recovered a single .40 S&W caliber discharged case in the grass. About two weeks after the Waffle House incident, on January 3, 2025, CMPD officers received a call for service for a shooting at the Market Express in Charlotte. Witnesses on the scene told officers that an individual later identified as Fuller came inside to get food at approximately 5:40 a.m. Fuller complained about a food order and argued with store employees. Fuller left the store and drove away. Later that same morning, at approximately 7:10 a.m., Fuller returned in his black Maserati, fired two times at one of the store employees, and fled. Officers arrived at the location and recovered two .40 S&W caliber shell casings on the ground. They also observed two large bullet holes in the windowpane to the left of the store’s door. Fuller was arrested on January 13, 2025, seated in the driver’s seat of the same black Maserati as the one driven during the shooting incidents. Trial evidence showed that the discharged cartridge casings seized as a result of the two incidents were both fired from the same firearm. Fuller has multiple prior felony convictions in North Carolina, including for distribution of cocaine, and he is prohibited from possessing a firearm or ammunition. The jury found Fuller guilty on two counts of possession of ammunition by a convicted felon. He faces a statutory sentence of up to 15 years in federal prison per count. A sentencing date has not been set. In making today’s announcement, U.S. Attorney Ferguson thanked the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, and the Charlotte-Mecklenburg Police Department for their investigation of the case. The U.S. Attorney’s Office in Charlotte is prosecuting the case. This case is part of Operation Take Back America , a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime. title: Daniel Sikkema Sentenced To Life In Prison For Murder-For-Hire Of His New York Art Gallerist Husband In Brazil
body: Press Release Daniel Sikkema Sentenced To Life In Prison For Murder-For-Hire Of His New York Art Gallerist Husband In Brazil Wednesday, November 4, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of New York United States Attorney for the Southern District of New York, Jamie McDonald, and Assistant Director in Charge of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (“FBI”), James C. Barnacle, Jr., announced today that DANIEL SIKKEMA was sentenced to life in prison for the January 14, 2024, murder of SIKKEMA’s husband, Brent Sikkema, in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, before U.S. District Judge Edgardo Ramos. SIKKEMA was convicted on May 22, 2026, following a two-week trial on charges of murder-for-hire, conspiracy to commit murder-for-hire, and conspiracy to commit murder in a foreign country. “Today’s life sentence holds Daniel Sikkema accountable for a cold, calculated murder-for-hire plot that resulted in the murder of his husband, Brent Sikkema,” said U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald. “For months, the defendant manipulated friends, family, and employees to execute a killing driven by greed. His actions demonstrated a profound disregard for human life and the rule of law. This sentence reflects the seriousness of the crime, and it reflects the strength and perseverance of the victim’s community and our law enforcement partners.” “Sikkema’s sick scheme to murder his estranged husband has culminated in a life behind bars,” said FBI Assistant Director in Charge James C. Barnacle, Jr. “The FBI and its law enforcement partners will continue to utilize every tool available to ensure that criminals who perpetrate the cruelest crimes have no way out. Justice will find you.” According to the Superseding Indictment, public court filings, and the evidence presented at trial: Beginning in 2023, SIKKEMA agreed to pay Alejandro Prevez to kill SIKKEMA’s estranged husband, Brent Sikkema, in Brazil. At that time, SIKKEMA and Brent Sikkema were engaged in contentious divorce proceedings, and Brent Sikkema, the owner of a well-known art gallery in Manhattan, regularly stayed at a residence he owned in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. To facilitate the murder-for-hire plot, SIKKEMA, a U.S. and Cuban citizen, sent eleven payments to Prevez and Prevez’s romantic interest in Cuba. SIKKEMA concealed the source of each of these payments by using the identities of unwitting friends, employees, and family members. On January 14, 2024, Prevez murdered Brent Sikkema at his residence in Rio de Janeiro by stabbing him 18 times. Minutes after the murder, Prevez called SIKKEMA multiple times on a secret phone number that SIKKEMA had arranged with Prevez to communicate about the murder plot. Shortly after the murder, SIKKEMA secretly sent a $5,000 payment to Prevez for the murder, with the promise of additional payments to come. On January 18, 2024, Prevez was arrested by Brazilian law enforcement for his involvement in the commission of Brent Sikkema’s murder. His criminal case remains pending in Brazilian courts. *                *                * In addition to prison, SIKKEMA, 56, of New York, New York, was sentenced to five years of supervised release. Mr. McDonald thanked the FBI New York Field Office. Mr. McDonald also expressed appreciation for the assistance of the FBI Legal Attaché Office in Brazil; the Criminal Division’s Human Rights and Special Prosecutions Section; the Criminal Division’s Office of International Affairs; the Civil Police of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil; the Federal Prosecutor’s Office of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil; the Military Police of Minas Gerais, Brazil; and the Fiscalía Provincial de Castellón, Spain. This case is being handled by the Office’s General Crimes Unit. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Meredith Foster, Remy Grosbard, Alexander Li, and Nicholas Pavlis are in charge of the prosecution, with assistance from paralegal specialists Mackenzie Ford and Olivia Sebade. Contact Nicholas Biase, Shelby Wratchford (212) 637-2600 Updated November 4, 2026 Component USAO - New York, Southern Press Release Number: 26-313

body: Take a closer look at art with the Courtauld Nov 04, 2026 | x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link The Art of Looking, a new project from Google Arts & Culture and the Courtauld, invites you to take a closer look at historic works of art. Mark Hallett and Amit Sood are launching The Art of Looking to expand our Courtauld partnership. You can explore twelve new stories that examine fundamental questions about art history and creative processes. These digital tools help people across the globe access detailed images and research from the gallery. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. Mark Hallett of the Courtauld Institute of Art and Amit Sood of Google Arts & Culture are launching The Art of Looking. This collection lets you zoom into famous paintings to see fine details, brushstrokes, and hidden stories from centuries of art history. You can explore these works online to learn how artists created their masterpieces. We are also starting an artist residency to use new technology for organizing and sharing these historic collections with everyone. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. Explore other styles: General summary Bullet points Basic explainer Today, we are delighted to launch ‘ The Art of Looking’ , a major expansion of the partnership between Google Arts & Culture and the Courtauld Institute of Art. This collection, which brings together art made across centuries and continents, reflects a shared commitment to opening up art and art history to the broadest possible audience, in keeping with the Courtauld’s commitment to art for all. Additionally, we’re jointly announcing a new artist residency to explore how AI can be used for metadata workflows in cultural institutions. The 12 new stories in ‘The Art of Looking’ take on some of the most fundamental questions we can ask about art. In ‘ What does art mean? ’ Professor Dorothy Price shows how the painter Lubaina Himid used her imagination to rewrite history, while in ‘ Who is art for? ’ Dr. Tom Stammers traces how artist Rosa Bonheur bypassed the elite gatekeepers of her day to reach a global audience. The stories also take us closer to how artists made the works themselves: zoom into the bold marks of Van Gogh’s reed pens, explore the enduring riddle of Michelangelo’s The Dream , or discover with Dr. Jessica Barker how Claudette Johnson uses the monumental scale of Blues Dance to give her subjects a powerful presence. Édouard Manet, “A Bar at the Folies-Bergère,” 1882 Manet’s last major painting depicts Suzon, a barmaid at the Folies-Bergère, who seems to embody a sense of detached melancholy at the heart of one of Paris’s most fashionable music halls. Much of the painting’s unsettling power lies in its mirror: ignoring normal perspective, Manet shifts the barmaid’s reflection to the right, so that she appears to be serving a male customer even while she gazes out, enigmatically, towards the viewer. Vincent Van Gogh, “Self-Portrait with Bandaged Ear,” 1889 Painted in Arles in January 1889, shortly after Van Gogh had cut off most of his left ear during a severe mental crisis, this self-portrait is at once a record of vulnerability and powerful proof of his determination to keep painting. Behind him, a canvas just begun and a Japanese print, one of his greatest sources of inspiration, point to the ambitions that sustained him. Claudette Johnson, “Blues Dance,” 2023 Claudette Johnson, a prominent figure of the British Black Arts Movement, made “Blues Dance” for her 2023 exhibition at the Courtauld Gallery, drawing on her memories of the Blue Beat dance scene of the 1980s. Its fluid, expressive lines and rich color celebrate music, movement, and joy, while its epic scale gives the dancing figure a commanding presence. Pieter Bruegel the Elder, “Landscape with the Flight into Egypt,” 1563 Bruegel sets the biblical story of the Holy Family’s flight into a grand, sweeping landscape, in which human drama is almost absorbed by the natural world. The small, vulnerable figures of Mary, Joseph, and the infant Jesus are tucked into this panoramic scene, emphasizing the power and scale of their surroundings. Founded in 1932 as the first institution in the UK devoted to the study of art history, the Courtauld is today an internationally renowned center for teaching and research, as well as a major public gallery. It is home to the largest community of art historians and conservators in the UK, and its scholars have long been pioneers in using technology, from X-rays to chemistry, to reveal what lies beneath the surface of works of art. Making its collection — and the research behind it — accessible to audiences across the globe remains a central priority. Google Arts & Culture first partnered with The Courtauld in 2022, using Google’s Art Camera to capture 16 iconic works in remarkable depth and detail. For the first time, anyone, anywhere could follow the extraordinary play of Manet’s brushstrokes across the surface of “A Bar at the Folies-Bergère”. title: AI Is Changing How Semiconductor Fabs Work — and Engineers Are Moving Faster Because of It
body: AI Is Changing How Semiconductor Fabs Work — and Engineers Are Moving Faster Because of It An AI-defined fab uses accelerated simulation, learned physics models and AI agents to give engineers faster answers across design, testing and manufacturing. November 3, 2026 by Timothy Costa 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Your browser doesn't support HTML5 video. Here is a link to the video instead. Demand for advanced chips is rising. The processes to build them are getting more complex. And the margin for error is shrinking. For engineers, understanding how a process change will behave, how a material will interact with a new step, how a defect maps back to a root cause are critical, challenging steps in semiconductor manufacturing — and these analyses can take days. Physical experiments on a fab line are slow and expensive. A wrong call on yield or process quality has real consequences. AI is transforming semiconductor manufacturing, impacting what engineers can do — and how fast. Accelerated computing shortens simulation time, allowing engineers to evaluate more alternatives before committing to physical trials. Physics-based AI helps engineers predict process behavior without running a full simulation every time. AI agents handle sequences of engineering tasks that once consumed hours. And digital twins let teams test changes in a virtual environment before committing to physical trials. Together, these capabilities describe an AI-defined fab: a semiconductor manufacturing factory where AI helps engineers optimize processes, catch problems earlier and make better decisions across the full manufacturing chip lifecycle. Engineers direct the work and make decisions based on their expertise while spending less time waiting for answers. Shorter Simulation Cycles Change What Engineers Can Explore Accelerated computing doesn’t just speed up individual calculations — it changes how many alternatives engineers can test before committing. Multiphysics simulations model interactions among physical effects, such as heat transfer, electrical behavior and mechanical stress. Using the NVIDIA cuDSS library, multiphysics software provider COMSOL is accelerating such simulations for semiconductor manufacturing by up to 10x. This helps engineers optimize equipment and processes, compare alternatives and decide which changes to test physically. Applied Materials and NVIDIA are collaborating to accelerate atomic-scale materials discovery and process development. By integrating NVIDIA cuDSS, Applied’s Ginestra simulation platform runs up to 10x faster than CPU-only approaches. And with NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo, Applied’s ACE+ multiphysics platform delivers topography simulations up to 35x faster. In some cases, acceleration doesn’t just shorten the calculation — it enables it altogether. Computational lithography — which defines how circuit patterns are printed onto silicon — involves calculations too intensive to complete on CPU at production scale. Siemens is integrating NVIDIA cuLitho into its Calibre lithography software, delivering up to 17x acceleration on key simulation workloads. That expands what engineers can verify before a wafer goes to print. As such, faster calculations can help researchers explore material behavior and reaction pathways that influence next-generation semiconductor processes. Predicting Process Behavior Without Running Every Simulation In addition to accelerating simulations, AI trained on physics can predict how materials and processes will behave — without running a full simulation each time. The payoff is most visible in complex calculations that are expensive even on accelerated hardware. Plasma — the electrically charged gas used in semiconductor etch processes — is one example. Modeling plasma behavior requires solving equations that capture how electrical, chemical and thermal processes interact, making repeated simulation costly. Lam Research demonstrated that the NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo framework can predict plasma behavior in milliseconds, compared with days for a full simulation — giving engineers a faster way to explore process conditions without rerunning the full model each time. Applied Materials uses digital twins built on NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to simulate fab-level optimizations in layout, throughput, cost and process control. Agents Handle the Steps Between Decisions Engineers turn analyses into decisions — revising a design, investigating a test failure, adjusting a production process and more. AI agents can help carry out the steps between those decisions. Evaluating which AI model to apply to a given task is one example: a sequential, manual process that can consume hours on the test floor. Advantest is using NVIDIA NeMo Switchyard AI agents to automate that selection, reducing response times from hours to minutes. Testing Factory Changes Before They Reach the Line Digital twins let teams simulate equipment configurations, layouts and process changes in a virtual environment before committing to physical trials. This reduces experimentation costs, especially as fabs become more complex and the stakes of a wrong change get higher. A photorealistic fab digital twin built with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries, used to simulate material flow, spot bottlenecks and validate operational strategies before deployment. Image courtesy of Applied Materials. Applied Materials uses NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to build physically accurate digital twins of entire fabs. Teams can simulate material movement, identify bottlenecks and evaluate layouts and operating strategies — extending virtual experimentation beyond individual processes to how the factory works as a whole. The Connected Loop The future of semiconductor manufacturing lies in connecting these capabilities: using production data to inform models and models to evaluate changes, then bringing those findings back to the engineers making production decisions. That’s the promise of the AI-defined fab: where AI helps people learn from each production cycle and act on that knowledge sooner. Explore how NVIDIA is working with semiconductor leaders across the chip lifecycle. And digital twins let teams test changes in a virtual environment before committing to physical trials. Together, these capabilities describe an AI-defined fab: a semiconductor manufacturing factory where AI helps engineers optimize processes, catch problems earlier and make better decisions across the full manufacturing chip lifecycle. Engineers direct the work and make decisions based on their expertise while spending less time waiting for answers. Shorter Simulation Cycles Change What Engineers Can Explore Accelerated computing doesn’t just speed up individual calculations — it changes how many alternatives engineers can test before committing. Multiphysics simulations model interactions among physical effects, such as heat transfer, electrical behavior and mechanical stress. Using the NVIDIA cuDSS library, multiphysics software provider COMSOL is accelerating such simulations for semiconductor manufacturing by up to 10x. This helps engineers optimize equipment and processes, compare alternatives and decide which changes to test physically. Applied Materials and NVIDIA are collaborating to accelerate atomic-scale materials discovery and process development. By integrating NVIDIA cuDSS, Applied’s Ginestra simulation platform runs up to 10x faster than CPU-only approaches. And with NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo, Applied’s ACE+ multiphysics platform delivers topography simulations up to 35x faster. In some cases, acceleration doesn’t just shorten the calculation — it enables it altogether. Computational lithography — which defines how circuit patterns are printed onto silicon — involves calculations too intensive to complete on CPU at production scale. Siemens is integrating NVIDIA cuLitho into its Calibre lithography software, delivering up to 17x acceleration on key simulation workloads. That expands what engineers can verify before a wafer goes to print. As such, faster calculations can help researchers explore material behavior and reaction pathways that influence next-generation semiconductor processes. Predicting Process Behavior Without Running Every Simulation In addition to accelerating simulations, AI trained on physics can predict how materials and processes will behave — without running a full simulation each time. The payoff is most visible in complex calculations that are expensive even on accelerated hardware. Plasma — the electrically charged gas used in semiconductor etch processes — is one example. Modeling plasma behavior requires solving equations that capture how electrical, chemical and thermal processes interact, making repeated simulation costly. Lam Research demonstrated that the NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo framework can predict plasma behavior in milliseconds, compared with days for a full simulation — giving engineers a faster way to explore process conditions without rerunning the full model each time. Applied Materials uses digital twins built on NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to simulate fab-level optimizations in layout, throughput, cost and process control. Agents Handle the Steps Between Decisions Engineers turn analyses into decisions — revising a design, investigating a test failure, adjusting a production process and more. AI agents can help carry out the steps between those decisions. Evaluating which AI model to apply to a given task is one example: a sequential, manual process that can consume hours on the test floor. Advantest is using NVIDIA NeMo Switchyard AI agents to automate that selection, reducing response times from hours to minutes. Testing Factory Changes Before They Reach the Line Digital twins let teams simulate equipment configurations, layouts and process changes in a virtual environment before committing to physical trials. This reduces experimentation costs, especially as fabs become more complex and the stakes of a wrong change get higher. A photorealistic fab digital twin built with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries, used to simulate material flow, spot bottlenecks and validate operational strategies before deployment. Image courtesy of Applied Materials. Applied Materials uses NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to build physically accurate digital twins of entire fabs. Teams can simulate material movement, identify bottlenecks and evaluate layouts and operating strategies — extending virtual experimentation beyond individual processes to how the factory works as a whole. The Connected Loop The future of semiconductor manufacturing lies in connecting these capabilities: using production data to inform models and models to evaluate changes, then bringing those findings back to the engineers making production decisions. That’s the promise of the AI-defined fab: where AI helps people learn from each production cycle and act on that knowledge sooner. Explore how NVIDIA is working with semiconductor leaders across the chip lifecycle.

body: New research shows how Guided Learning supports students Nov 03, 2026 | x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Two new studies show how Guided Learning boosts student performance, plus new Google Classroom features that give teachers more control. We are rolling out Guided Learning in Google Classroom to help students master difficult topics step by step. Instead of giving direct answers, this tool coaches students through complex concepts, practice quizzes, and custom visual aids. Research shows this approach helps students learn more effectively during independent study. Teachers can now assign these guided lessons, track student progress, and spend more time providing one-on-one support where it is needed most. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Explore other styles: General summary Bullet points Basic explainer We’re sharing two new studies that show how Guided Learning supports students and teachers in real-world settings. Alongside these findings, today we’re starting to roll out Guided Learning in Google Classroom , giving teachers even more control over how and when this tool is used in their classrooms. Guided Learning is designed to help students work through complex concepts step by step, prioritizing deep understanding over providing direct answers. Boosting statistics scores To see how Guided Learning impacts real performance, we conducted a randomized controlled trial (RCT) with more than 300 students at the University of Tokyo. We wanted to test whether Guided Learning provided extra value beyond standard study tools. All students were given half a day to independently study a statistics lesson using standard online resources. Half of the group was also given access to Guided Learning in the Gemini app. Instead of looking for quick answers, students used Guided Learning to dig deeper. They frequently asked for practice quizzes, step-by-step help, and custom visual aids. When we compared pre- and post-test scores, the difference was clear. Students using only standard web tools improved their scores by 5.3 percentage points. But students with access to Guided Learning improved by 8.1 percentage points, representing 1.5x higher learning gains in just a single study session. While that number might seem modest — these gains were achieved in just half a day of study, pointing to growing evidence that when technology guides students rather than shortcutting the process, it can lead to more learning. Giving teachers more insight and control Bringing Guided Learning into Google Classroom requires a specialized approach that is purpose-built for the classroom, keeps teachers in control, and grounds the experience in relevant lesson materials. To test this experience, we partnered with Ark and ran a four-week pilot across three UK secondary schools, allowing teachers to use Guided Learning in Google Classroom across four different subjects. Feedback from post-pilot surveys and interviews was encouraging: teachers found Guided Learning handled initial student questions effectively during independent work, so they had more time to offer targeted, one-on-one help. Meanwhile, the majority of surveyed students said they felt comfortable asking Gemini for help when stuck, and over half said it helped them solve problems on their own. We also received important feedback on areas of improvement. Some teachers wanted clearer visibility into how their students were engaging with the course materials so they could better tailor future lessons. Others voiced a desire to keep their students focused on specific assignments during class time and reduce distractions. We took this feedback back to the team and made direct improvements — including adding insights for educators to show how their students interacted with Guided Learning, and improving the ability for teachers to anchor conversations on uploaded curriculum. Shaped by real educator and student feedback in the classroom, today we're rolling out teacher-led Guided Learning globally in Google Classroom. This feature will help teachers assign their students a Guided Learning experience that will coach students step-by-step on their course materials and track student progress with actionable insights. By grounding our tools in learning science, working alongside educators, and conducting research in real classroom settings, we're eager to continue innovating on tools that support active learning and a deeper understanding. We are introducing Guided Learning to Google Search and Google Classroom to support active student problem solving. Chris Phillips, VP and General Manager of Education, explains that we are adding Guided Learning to Google Search and Classroom to help students think through problems instead of just finding quick answers. This tool acts like a personal coach, using questions to guide students through complex topics step by step. We are also giving school administrators full control to decide which AI tools are available to their students, ensuring technology supports classroom learning. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. Explore other styles: General summary Bullet points Basic explainer If you’ve ever watched a student use AI tools to help with their schoolwork, you’ve probably wondered: Are they actually learning, or just finding a shortcut? Questions like this are important, and they guide our work when building products for learning. We believe technology paired with great educators can unlock incredible learning potential, and we’re focused on building technology responsibly to help students thrive. Today, we’re making important updates to our products used in schools, including building Guided Learning capabilities into Google Search and Google Classroom, and evolving our approach to school controls. Developing products built for learning We believe AI products should support “productive struggle” — enabling students to be actively challenged without getting so overwhelmed that they give up. That’s the philosophy behind Guided Learning. In Gemini, Guided Learning acts as an interactive study tool that coaches students through the process of problem solving through open-ended questions and step-by-step breakdowns. Our research shows that Guided Learning leads to measurable learning gains for students, and we’re now bringing Guided Learning to more products. Google Search: We’re building Guided Learning capabilities into Search for student accounts to help them work through problems without skipping straight to answers. When our systems understand a student is looking for certain types of homework help, Search will walk them through the topic or problem step by step. For example, if a student pastes a complex physics problem or asks for help writing a book report in Search, they’ll see prompts to help them think critically and work through the concepts, without going directly to the answer. We’re starting with a pilot in select U.S. schools later this month to gather and incorporate educator feedback before expanding to other school districts in the coming months. Google Classroom: Starting today, Guided Learning is globally available in Google Classroom, a central hub where teachers and students organize schoolwork, share assignments and stay connected. When a student starts a Guided Learning activity assigned by their teacher, it acts like a 1-1 study tool, anchored in class material to help them stay on task. It also gives teachers real-time insights to spot where the class might need extra support. Before launching Guided Learning in Google Classroom, we worked closely with schools and educators to test the feature and integrate their feedback. Enhancing school controls We believe schools should have control over AI in their classrooms and in providing administrators with controls to help them manage their approach. After listening to schools, teachers, leading researchers, and policymakers, we are now updating our approach to controls for Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Google Search. Access to these products will be entirely off for K-12 student accounts until school administrators explicitly turn them on. We’ll share more specifics with schools in the coming months ahead of the changes rolling out so they have time to prepare and enable a smooth transition. Our goal is simple: provide school leaders the control and confidence to use AI products in classrooms as they see fit. We’ll continue to listen to feedback and evolve our approach as we work in partnership with schools, teachers, pedagogical experts, and parents on helping the next generation learn and thrive. body: Expanding AI educator training to new countries Nov 03, 2026 | x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link The Google AI Educator Series is expanding to five new countries: Spain, Brazil, Mexico, Australia, and sub-Saharan Africa. Here’s how teachers are already using it around the globe. Jennie Magiera Global Head of Education Impact Share x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Read AI-generated summary We created the Google AI Educator Series to provide teachers with practical skills for using AI. Our training program is currently available in several countries and will soon reach more regions. Educators use these tools to create engaging lessons, save time on tasks, and support student learning. We are launching new November modules to help teachers build assessments and guide game-based learning activities. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. Teachers around the world strive to find better ways to overcome challenges and meet each students' unique needs, and many have discovered how AI can become a powerful assistant in this effort. That's why we created the Google AI Educator Series (GES): a no-cost, on-demand training designed to give educators practical AI skills they can use immediately and that fits into their busy schedule. We first launched GES in the U.S earlier this year , and later expanded to India , Korea , Malaysia , Philippines, and the U.K & Ireland. In the coming months, we’re bringing GES to Brazil, Mexico, Spain, Australia, and sub-Saharan Africa. A look at GES from teachers around the world Here is a look at how educators around the world are turning their training into practical applications that save time, make lessons more engaging, and support student learning: India: Teachers are using Gemini and Gemini Notebook to turn complex topics into comic strips, podcasts & infographics – making learning more accessible and engaging. Following September sessions that trained 80,000 educators, we’re bringing GES to all Indian educators with self-paced online modules . Aligned with National Education Policy 2020 , the training is available in English & six local languages — Hindi, Marathi, Telugu, Assamese, Odia, Punjabi — with more coming next year. Philippines: Educators are using Gemini to simulate complex market scenarios in economics classes and more, all to free up time for direct student guidance. To support this progress, we’ve partnered with the Philippine Department of Education , Commission on Higher Education , and Technical Skills Development Authority to bring AI training to over one million educators across the country. Building on this momentum, the Philippine Department of Education recently issued an official memorandum endorsing GES to all teaching and non-teaching staff nationwide. Malaysia: Following the official launch of GES at BETT Asia , Malaysian teachers report saving three to five hours of prep time on curricula, assessments, and visual aids per topic, allowing them to focus on interactive, student-centered learning. As a next step, we are launching "train-the-trainer" bootcamps alongside local partners to expand GES training to private school educators , pre-service teachers , and university faculty nationwide. United Kingdom: In the U.K ., teachers are using tools like Gemini Notebook to develop learners’ creative writing skills and create engaging lesson plans and visuals. Through the launch of GES, all 650,000 teachers can receive digital literacy training by joining virtual or in-person events around the UK and Ireland. We are also hosting “ train the trainer ” workshops in the Google London office in November. Korea: In partnership with Seoul National University of Education (SNUE), GES in Korea is aligned with the 2022 Revised Curriculum and the Ministry of Education's Teacher AI/Digital Education Competency Framework. Teachers are using Gemini and Gemini Notebook to design inquiry-based lessons and assessments while streamlining administrative tasks like parent communications and data analysis. New November sessions To ensure GES lessons are truly helpful, we update and create new content monthly in response to feedback from educators. Our November modules go live on November 4th in the U.S. focused on helping educators save time where they tell us they need it most. Here's what's coming: Build interactive assessments: Learn how to use Gemini to build practice tests and interactive web assessments — like exit tickets with instant feedback and hints for incorrect answers — to help students prepare for assessments like state exams.. Guide students through game-based learning: Guide students through interactive, game-based learning experiences that demonstrate the importance of data accuracy, model performance, and human oversight. Strengthen academic assignments: Use Gemini to learn how to spot questions that can lead to taking shortcuts, helping faculty strengthen assignments and encourage deeper student critical thinking. These efforts include AI-driven call detection, threat intelligence sharing, and 6 million dollars in funding to help people and small businesses stay safe online. You can learn more about these initiatives and access scam prevention resources through our latest updates on the Google Safety Center. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. We are scaling our defenses across Asia Pacific to protect people from complex, organized scam networks. New Android features like Fake Call Detection help you identify AI-driven impersonation and malicious mobile applications. We joined the Industry Accord Against Online Scams and Fraud to share threat intelligence with peers. Google.org is providing $6 million in funding to help small businesses and individuals build scam resilience. We are strengthening our defenses against complex scams across the Asia Pacific region. Our new Android features now detect AI-driven impersonation calls and alert you to suspicious messages. We are also working with industry partners to share threat intelligence and providing 6 million dollars in funding to local organizations. These efforts help you, small businesses, and communities recognize fraud, stay safe online, and build resilience against organized crime groups. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. Explore other styles: General summary Bullet points Basic explainer Scams are growing more complex, fueled by increasingly sophisticated tactics from transnational crime groups. A recent UN report illustrated the effect these scams have across the Asia Pacific (APAC) region. In 2025, scam losses across East Asia, Southeast Asia, Australia, and New Zealand reached up to $114.1 billion USD, with over 40% of ASEAN consumers said to be experiencing scams. Tackling these highly organized networks requires a unified effort. Today, we are sharing how, at Google, we are scaling our defenses to protect APAC communities. This includes built-in protections across products and platforms, industry-wide collaboration, and new local partnerships to increase community resilience. Built-in protections across devices and platforms Our first line of defense is to secure the devices and platforms people use every day. This year, Android launched Fake Call Detection , a feature designed to spot AI-driven phone call impersonation. Built on open RCS technology, other platforms can adopt the same protections. On Pixel, built-in scam detection now alerts you to potential scams from many popular messaging apps. We are partnering to bring this to additional Android users later this year . We are also expanding Android developer verification to protect people against malicious apps outside Google Play, wherever apps are distributed. Industry alignment for collective defense Beyond product solutions, defeating fraud networks requires coordination across experts and industries. Earlier this year, we joined industry peers to sign the Industry Accord Against Online Scams and Fraud , taking a collective approach to sharing threat intelligence and coordinating defenses. Building on the Industry Accord, we recently helped establish the Japan Anti-Scam Alliance (JASA) to enable public and private institutions to deploy aligned defenses. Google.org also recently helped launch the Global Anti-Scams Philanthropy Collaborative to coordinate cross-industry philanthropic action against scams globally. Efforts to strengthen community resilience To strengthen resilience at the community level, today Google.org announced $6 million in funding to The Asia Foundation and the Tech for Good Institute to help small businesses and individuals in APAC to stay safe online. The efforts will include training local communities on building scam resilience, incubating AI-powered defense prototypes, and equipping policymakers with insights to strengthen threat measures. This builds on Google.org’s ongoing support for local organizations, like Bamboo Builders in Singapore and the Taiwan FactCheck Center, to deliver specialized, hyper-local training to citizens. And it expands on the ASEAN Foundation’s Scam Ready ASEAN initiative, which is bringing online scam prevention resources to millions in the region. We are also expanding Be Scam Ready , an educational scam-awareness game — and one of the Scam Ready ASEAN’s program resources — to Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, the Philippines, and Vietnam. Be Scam Ready simulates common scams to prepare citizens, and is already available in Singapore, Thailand, and Taiwan. Helping communities stay ahead of organized fraud is central to our work, and we will continue to advocate for a collaborative, global approach. By clicking ‘Accept recommended settings’ on this banner, you accept our use of analytics cookies.   For more information on how these cookies work please see our Cookie policy . Accept recommended cookies Proceed with necessary cookies only Skip to main content Regulators explore credit union reforms to support growth, innovation and better outcomes for members Credit unions could benefit from several ideas put forward today by the Prudential Regulation Authority and Financial Conduct Authority aimed at helping the sector grow, innovate and meet the changing needs of their members. Published on  
        03 November 2026 News release Credit unions could benefit from several ideas put forward today by the Prudential Regulation Authority (PRA) and Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) aimed at helping the sector grow, innovate and meet the changing needs of their members. Credit unions, which are member-owned and typically focus on savings and personal loans in a specific occupation, community or area, have over two million members in the UK. Building on the joint PRA and FCA 2025 Mutuals Landscape report, this discussion paper examines whether the regulatory framework remains proportionate as the sector evolves, and explores how credit unions can expand access to financial services and improve outcomes for the members they serve. Options the regulators are seeking views on include: Removing some requirements on internal audit and regulatory documents for smaller credit unions, cutting red tape without compromising stability; Creating a risk-based framework for larger, more complex credit unions, giving them more flexible capital requirements; Applying relevant rules for smaller deposit takers, such as the standardised approach for risk weighted assets, to replace the current simple leverage ratio they report on; Applying a simplified version of the Basel framework, streamlining capital add-ons for large credit unions with specific exposures, and applying a simple capital buffer for absorbing shocks in stress periods; What barriers there are to credit unions offering new products and services, including how shared-service organisations and third-party organisations can best support investment, technology and operational capability; Giving credit unions additional guidance on FCA expectations around working with third-parties to provide important services; Whether changes to FCA fees could reduce regulatory costs and support sustainable growth; Providing credit unions a path to convert into building societies, bringing the benefits of a framework more tailored to specific lending and a wider range of funding tools; Reviewing the current framework for solvent exit, providing further flexibility to transfer business or restructure in an orderly manner. Shoib Khan, Director of UK Deposit Takers at the Prudential Regulation Authority, said: “Credit unions are a vital part of our financial services sector, and we have scope to make their regime even more proportionate and growth-friendly. We want to have an open, transparent dialogue with firms, and I look forward to seeing their honest feedback.” Sheree Howard, Executive Director of Authorisations at the Financial Conduct Authority, said: “Credit unions provide valuable support to millions of members, including many who may otherwise struggle to access affordable financial services. As the sector evolves, it is important that the regulatory framework keeps pace, enabling credit unions to innovate, grow and meet the changing needs of their members while continuing to deliver good outcomes for consumers. We want to hear directly from the sector about what is working well, where barriers remain, and how the regulatory framework may need to adapt to support a strong, sustainable future for credit unions.” The regulators are encouraging firms to offer their feedback on the options presented and whether there are other options which have not been included. The possibilities at this stage give more options to firms with very different business models, growth trajectories and risk profiles. Notes to editors Read the full Discussion Paper . Today’s announcement builds on a joint report released by the regulators on the wider mutuals sector, which outlined measures to support the sector’s growth and resilience. title: Cities Worldwide Build and Scale AI Services With NVIDIA Physical and Agentic AI
body: Cities Worldwide Build and Scale AI Services With NVIDIA Physical and Agentic AI From infrastructure planning and transportation to public services, cities are using NVIDIA-powered applications to address local needs and expand capacity for the broader AI ecosystem. November 2, 2026 by Esther Lee 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Cities generate enormous amounts of data from cameras, sensors and operational systems, but turning it into useful action — for planning, maintenance and public services — remains a challenge. Physical and agentic AI offer new ways to close that gap, from digital twins for infrastructure planning to vision and service agents, while keeping local governments in control of how sensitive data is processed and used. Building on initiatives announced at GTC Berlin , NVIDIA and its partners are expanding physical AI and AI agents to cities worldwide. Shared computing infrastructure gives city departments, neighboring municipalities and local developers a common foundation to build on — extending services without each organization having to acquire and manage resources of their own. Agentic AI for Cities From resident services to vision agents, cities are adopting NVIDIA agentic AI to deliver faster, more responsive public services. City teams don’t need a massive infrastructure investment to get started building these AI services: depending on the workload, NVIDIA RTX workstations or a small GPU system may be enough. In Spain, 1MillionBot combines open source ALIA models trained at the Barcelona Supercomputing Center with NVIDIA Nemotron and other models in resident-service agents for Madrid Digital (Comunidad de Madrid), Administració Oberta de Catalunya and 150+ deployments across Spain, handling municipal procedures, appointment requests, urban-planning incidents and service inquiries. In the San Francisco Bay Area , LiveX is bringing its AI City vision to life with NVIDIA Cosmos world models and Nemotron open models, and Omniverse and Metropolis libraries on NVIDIA RTX PRO GPUs. The interactive, conversational AI hosts understand people’s needs, provide answers and take action, and can be tailored to local languages and service needs in airports, hospitals, local events and other public spaces. Vision AI agents can turn existing city camera feeds into operational insights, helping teams identify mobility and safety issues and coordinate emergency responses across city services. In Wrocław, Poland , K2K is building shared AI infrastructure using NVIDIA accelerated computing, NVIDIA Cosmos world reasoning models, and NVIDIA Metropolis Blueprint for video search and summarization (VSS) to transform existing camera streams into actionable intelligence for mobility, safety and event response — using the same infrastructure across several city functions. In Malaysia , ITMAX bundles infrastructure and agentic AI applications into long-term managed services for cities, including for traffic management. Built with reference to Cosmos, Nemotron and the Metropolis VSS blueprint, ITMAX’s SamurAI V2 vision agents are scaling on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPUs to support 17,000+ cameras by 2027. ITMAX integrates TeraSim, an open source traffic simulation platform from Laplace Intelligence , to test signal timing, reducing peak-hour corridor travel times by up to 26%. Plan and Operate Critical Infrastructure With Digital Twins Beyond public-facing services, digital twins can help cities expedite infrastructure planning, minimizing disruption to local communities. City digital twins can also serve as a real-time operational simulation to facilitate faster decision-making. At Dangote’s Lekki refinery in Nigeria, Honeywell Technologies’ Forge Plant Cognition uses Nemotron-powered AI agents to understand operational data. A digital twin of the plant and its processes, built using Omniverse libraries, is also planned to support simulation and training. The platform, built on Dell PowerEdge servers with NVIDIA RTX PRO accelerators, helps operators identify bottlenecks, anticipate equipment and process issues, and optimize plant performance. In Taiwan , Linker Vision and Dutch architecture firm MVRDV are using NVIDIA Omniverse and Nemotron to build environmental, social and governance agents that can assess the environmental impact of various urban planning scenarios, simulating 15-year outcomes of an urban forest canopy in 10 minutes — increasing design iteration speed from two weeks per iteration to less than an hour. Build a Broader Local AI Ecosystem Cities can extend AI to more services by building on infrastructure already in place and adding capacity. Shared resources and managed services can help extend those capabilities across departments and municipalities. At Morocco’s Tanger Med port, Cires Technologies is expanding a sovereign AI factory for planned applications in worker safety, congestion analysis, cargo routing and port operations. Cires Technologies is also building an ecosystem of application providers to develop local models and applications for ports and cities. Beyond city services, Barcelona Supercomputing Center’s AI Factory Accelerator Programme gives startups access to sovereign computing, technical support and training. BSC AI Factory also supports research and innovation for startups — spanning agriculture, medical imaging, knowledge access and speech services. Learn how NVIDIA and its ecosystem are bringing physical AI, agentic AI and local AI factories to cities worldwide at Smart City Expo World Congress, running Nov. 3-5 in Barcelona, where NVIDIA Vice President of EMEA Paolo Guglielmini will deliver a keynote address followed by a panel moderated by Charbel Aoun, director of smart city and spaces for EMEA at NVIDIA. title: Advancing research and partnering with universities in Singapore
body: Advancing research and partnering with universities in Singapore Nov 03, 2026 | x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Along with a new research hub in Singapore, Google is deepening its academic partnerships in the country with more than $6 million in grants for NUS and NTU — driving breakthroughs in AI for science and compute efficiency, strengthening AI safety frameworks, and nurturing scientific leaders. Yossi Matias Vice President, Google and General Manager, Google Research Share x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link Your browser does not support the audio element. Listen to article [[duration]] minutes This content is generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental Voice Speed Voice Speed 0.75X 1X 1.5X 2X Read AI-generated summary We are providing new research grants to universities in Singapore to support scientific discovery. This funding helps researchers study Alzheimer’s disease, improve computing efficiency, and build safer artificial intelligence systems. By investing in these local institutions, we are helping students and scientists develop the tools needed to solve complex global problems. You can expect these partnerships to foster new breakthroughs in medicine, technology, and human well-being. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. Technology is already transforming how we approach the world’s toughest challenges, and continuing that momentum requires supporting the people driving foundational science. With our newly established research hub in Singapore , and as we continue to scale existing health research initiatives in the country — including bringing open models like MedGemma to frontline care settings — Google is also deepening its academic partnerships in Singapore by investing over $6 million in new research grants and capacity-building initiatives at National University of Singapore (NUS) and Nanyang Technological University (NTU). Backing foundational and applied breakthroughs Our targeted grants address both urgent biomedical frontiers and the core building blocks of computing: Alzheimer’s research ($1.5 million grant — NUS) : Selected from over 3,500 global applications, NUS has been awarded an AI for Science Google.org Impact Challenge Grant to advance breakthroughs in neurodegenerative disease research using AI models and data science. Computing efficiency and regional languages ($500,000 grant — NUS) : This funding supports machine learning efficiency — focusing on sustainable compute and model serving optimization — and regional language processing. AI safety and security ($340,000 grant — NTU) : We are funding four sponsored research studies at NTU focused on advancing AI safety frameworks, robust evaluation methodologies, trustworthy multi-agent systems, and privacy-preserving LLM watermarking. The Google team met with NUS leadership, including Senior Vice Provost Prof. Bernard Tan and Dean of Computing Prof. Tulika Mitra, to align on new research infrastructure and cross-disciplinary workstreams. Building capacity for research ecosystem and future scholars Beyond individual research projects, true ecosystem enablement requires investing in long-term institutional infrastructure and talent pipelines. At NTU, a $750,000 AI for Science Capacity Fund Grant will help build permanent research capabilities across Southeast Asia. Under Professor Ho Teck Hua’s regional academic leadership, this initiative will establish lasting infrastructure, foster internal research agents, and build ethical AI frameworks that elevate the region’s scientific capacity. Google.org and Google DeepMind are also providing $3 million in funding to support INSEAD’s Thrive Lab in Singapore, which aims to advance global research into how people and organizations can thrive alongside rapid technological change. The lab will explore how education, workplaces, and communities can better support people to develop skills, find purpose, and build meaningful relationships in a changing world. This human-centered research sits alongside a broader wave of scientific breakthroughs driving the region forward. Whether unlocking insights into neurodegenerative diseases, making models more efficient and inclusive of local languages, or establishing safe research infrastructure, Singapore’s academic community continues to set a global benchmark for innovation. We are proud to enable with our tools and models the faculty, researchers, and students who are not just experimenting with AI, but preparing to lead the next era of scientific progress The Google team met with the NTU Deputy President & Provost, Prof Christian Wolfrum and colleagues to discuss partnerships across frontier research and AI safety, science, and education.
